Fixes alkem-io/server#6763

## Root cause

`applyForEntryRoleOnRoleSet` stored a new application with an **empty** authorization policy (four saves across `ApplicationService.createApplication`, `RoleSetService.createApplication` and the resolver) and only afterwards filled it in, through `resetAuthorizationsOnRoleSetApplicationsInvitations`. That pass recomputes the policy of *every* application, invitation and platform invitation on the role set and writes them all in one `saveAll` at the end, with no transaction around create + pass.

So any throw while computing the policy of an unrelated sibling — or the process dying in between — writes nothing, and the new application keeps zero credential rules. From then on every READ of it throws `AUTHORIZATION_INVALID_POLICY` (`AuthorizationService.validateAuthorization`), and because `Application.actor` and `RoleSet.applications` are non-nullable, one such row takes down the whole Community admin query.

## Producer proven

A sibling application on the same role set that is deleted after the pass has loaded the role set's applications but before the pass reaches it: `ApplicationAuthorizationService.extendAuthorizationPolicy` calls `applicationService.getActor(sibling.id)`, which throws `EntityNotFoundException`, the pass aborts, and nothing is saved.

Which producer hit production is **not known** — production data and logs were not inspected. The fix does not depend on which one it was: it removes the window instead of guarding one cause.

## The fix

- `ApplicationService.createApplication` builds the entity (user, empty policy, lifecycle) and no longer persists it.
- `ApplicationAuthorizationService.extendAuthorizationPolicy` uses `application.user` when it is already loaded, else falls back to `getActor(application.id)` as before.
- `RoleSetService.createApplication` attaches the role set, applies the policy against `roleSet.authorization`, then saves **once**.
- `applyForEntryRoleOnRoleSet` drops the redundant extra save and the role-set-wide pass. An application's policy is the role set's cascading rules plus the applicant's own rule; a new application changes no other entity's policy, so the pass had nothing else to do here.

Net: four writes of a half-built row become one write of a complete row. No migration, no GraphQL schema change, the READ guard is untouched.

## Regression test

`src/domain/access/role-set/role.set.resolver.mutations.membership.apply.policy.spec.ts` runs the real resolver, `RoleSetService`, `RoleSetAuthorizationService`, `ApplicationService`, `ApplicationAuthorizationService`, `AuthorizationPolicyService` and `AuthorizationService`; only the repositories are replaced, by a store that keeps what each write persisted.

- `never persists an application whose policy has no credential rules`
- `leaves the new application readable when another application on the role set cannot have its policy applied`

Before the fix both fail; the second with the exact production error:

```
AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 0
AssertionError: expected [Function] to not throw an error but
"AuthorizationPolicy without credential rules provided: policy-2, type: application, privilege: read, message: Application.actor" was thrown
```

Control: with the sibling deletion removed, the second test passes on the old code — the sibling failure is what discriminates. After the fix both pass.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Make the READ guard tolerate an empty application policy** — hides the broken row (admins would silently lose the application) instead of preventing it.
- **Wrap create + role-set-wide pass in a transaction** — keeps four writes and keeps one applicant's request failing because of an unrelated sibling; more machinery to preserve a pass this flow does not need.
- **Catch per-entity errors inside the pass** — a guard around a mechanism that should not run here, and it would swallow real failures during authorization resets, which share that code.
- **Repair existing rows with a migration** — out of scope; see below.

## Gates

- `pnpm lint` (tsc --noEmit + biome): pass
- `pnpm build`: pass
- `pnpm test:ci:no:coverage`: 911 files passed, 13 skipped; 12225 tests passed, 57 skipped

## Not verified

- Not run against a live database or a running server; the single cascading insert is covered by unit-level tests only. Its shape (application + new policy + questions in one save) is the same as the first save of the old flow.
- If the single save fails, the lifecycle row created just before it is left orphaned (previously the half-built application was left as well).

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

- Rows already stored with an empty policy are not repaired by this change. `authorizationPolicyResetOnAccount` for the owning account re-applies them; if it fails, its error names the entity that breaks the pass.
- The invitation and platform-invitation create paths (`inviteForEntryRoleOnRoleSet`) still store entities with an empty policy and rely on the same shared pass, so they have the same window. They should get the same treatment in their own change.

Fixes alkem-io/server#5913

## Summary

Members who sign in with a password can protect their account with an authenticator app, security keys and recovery codes, all managed by Kratos. The platform rule (for platform roles) and an organisation's rule decide who must use a second factor. After a grace period, a covered person who has not used one is refused with a dedicated error code, on open subscriptions too, until they enrol and sign in again. Support can reset a member's second factor through an audited mutation, which can also make the password unusable. Every rule switch, reset and factor change is recorded, and the member is emailed when their second factor changes.

## Root cause

alkem-io/server#5913: Kratos MFA was not enabled, and the server had no notion of an account's assurance level. The server slice of workspace#103 keeps the sign-in's assurance level on the session, enforces the requirement where a sign-in credential becomes an actor, and adds the reset and the audit trail the spec requires.

## Fix

The assurance level is read from the `acr` of the validated ID token or access token. A per-request policy evaluates the platform and organisation rules from the database, reading both in parallel, and fails closed when a rule cannot be read. A second-factor-required error code is enforced in the auth interceptor and before each subscription event. The requirement status is exposed for the signed-in person. The support reset removes factors, ends Kratos and application sessions, and can replace the password twice; it writes intent and outcome rows. A consumer records each factor change that Kratos reports and publishes the change notice. That publish is awaited, bounded at five seconds and not retried after a timeout, so a broker outage neither hangs the reset nor sends the member the same notice more than once. The audit analysis tool counts a failed second-factor reset as an anomaly. Includes additive enum migrations and local Kratos and Hydra configuration.

## Tests

Unit specs cover the policy, interceptor, strategies, subscription re-validation and audit writer. They also cover the change observer, including a timed-out notice that is published once and recorded as a timeout. The reset service specs check step order, both password replacements, every failure arm, and logging before the fail-closed row. The notification adapter specs cover an accepted, a rejected and a stalled publish. The audit analysis tool spec checks that a failed reset is flagged as an anomaly.

## Verification

- New timed-out-notice spec: RED when every error is retried (3 publishes), green when a TimeoutError is not retried
- New audit-analysis anomaly spec: RED without SECOND_FACTOR_RESET_FAILED in the anomaly set, green with it

**Do not merge until matrix-adapter v0.8.28 is released and deployed (alkem-io/matrix-adapter#99), and this branch bumps `@alkemio/matrix-adapter-lib` to 0.8.28 in both `package.json` and the lockfile (OG-5). Until then CI cannot resolve `COMMUNICATION_ACTOR_SESSIONS_REVOKE`. It is open for review now; CI goes green once the lib is bumped.**

User deletion now revokes the user's Matrix devices (FR-017).

**`CommunicationAdapter.revokeActorSessions(actorID)`**
- Sends `{ actor_id }` on `COMMUNICATION_ACTOR_SESSIONS_REVOKE`, the same way `createActorSession` sends its request.
- Returns the number of devices revoked.
- Returns 0 when communications are disabled.

**`UserService.revokeUserSessionsAndIdentity`**
- Calls it alongside the OIDC and Kratos revocations, so both the admin delete and the self-service account-deletion paths are covered.
- Calls it **before** the `authenticationID` guard, so a user whose authentication ID was already cleared is still covered (review fix ENG-091-SRV-01 / SEC-091-SRV-01).
- Best-effort:
  - a failure is logged as `Failed to revoke Matrix sessions during user deletion; the deletion still stands`;
  - the failure is recorded as `sessionRevocationSucceeded = false`;
  - the deletion itself is never undone.

**Tests:**
- `revokeActorSessions sends the actor id on the sessions revoke topic`
- `revokes the user's Matrix sessions when the user is deleted`
- `a failed Matrix revocation marks session revocation failed and the deletion still stands`
- The test for a user without an authentication ID now also expects the Matrix call.

484 tests pass, and typecheck and biome are clean. They ran against a lib built locally from alkem-io/matrix-adapter#99.

**Residual R-12:** if matrix-adapter or Synapse is unreachable during the deletion, the devices survive until their tokens expire. The infrastructure-operations runbook covers removing them by hand.

## Workspace

`workspace#091-matrix-session-hardening`. The spec, plan and residual analysis are in the private agents-hq repo. Story: alkem-io/client-web#10463 (epic alkem-io/alkemio#2134).

**Why.** Matrix calls dropped about every 48 h. Synapse issued a token with a fixed expiry, and on expiry the client recovered onto a new device, which ended the call and reloaded the chats. With this feature the client renews a short-lived token in place on the same client, so a renewal never drops a call. Matrix devices are also ended when the Alkemio session ends and when the account is deleted.

**Merge order:** dev-orchestration → infrastructure-operations → matrix-adapter (then release v0.8.28 and deploy) → client-web → server.

## Summary

Data repair for space roles whose `credential.resourceID` points at a **different space**. Cause: `RoleService.createRole` aliased the module-level role definitions, and `updateRoleResourceID` mutated them in place during recursive template-subspace creation. efb6d8ea8 (#6467) fixed this for new data only. On acceptance: 162 roles on 54 spaces, 167 issued credentials, and 6,414 stored policies that grant one space's privileges to members of another.

```text
up()                                    (one transaction, every change logged)
  1. role.credential.resourceID := owning space id               162 roles
  2. for each credential (type, wrong target) issued via those roles
       owner evidence  = member-joined in owner within 60s | invitation/application on owner
       target evidence = same tests against the target
       owner evidence              -> grant (type, owner) if missing   164
       owner && !target evidence   -> revoke (type, target)            163
         except membership kept if holder is in a subspace of target     1
       target space deleted        -> revoke
       no evidence either way      -> untouched, logged 'ambiguous'      0
  3. space-subspace-admin re-derived for the owners                18 moved
  4. parentCredentials recomputed in the owners' subtrees          420 roles
  5. any mis-pointed role left -> throw (rollback)
down()  replays _repair_mispointed_role_credentials in reverse
```

**Post-deploy (required):** run `mutation { authorizationPolicyResetAll }` and let it drain, because stored policies keep the old grants until the reset. Flush the role-set membership cache, or wait for `collaboration.membership.cache_ttl` (4h).

## Evidence

Run on a restored copy of the acceptance DB (2026-11-04), measured with the data-consistency suite (1,149 read-only checks):

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `auth-role-space-resourceid-mismatch` | 162 | 0 |
| `…mispointed-role-creds-issued` | 167 | 0 |
| `…mispointed-role-creds-holder-without-owner-cred` | 164 | 0 |
| `…space-policies-crit-from-mispointed-role` | 6,414 | 0 |
| `…space-l2-role-parentcredentials-missing-l0` | 464 | 74 (outside the affected subtrees) |

- No check errors, and nothing changes outside the role and credential domains.
- `…crit-other-space-residual` rises from 422 to 6,836. That is expected: the stored policies still carry the old rules until the reset.
- `up()` takes 0.5 s. A second `up()` is a no-op.
- `down()` restores `credential` + `role` to an md5-identical copy of the original.
- The spec (`__tests__/1791400000000-…spec.ts`) has 5 passing tests: no-op when clean, log-before-write ordering, rollback on residual, and `down()` covering every action.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Every change is logged, and `migration:revert` restores the exact prior rows. The policies are recomputed by the reset either way.

## Summary

A visual's picture can no longer be pointed at an outside host through updateVisual. Any non-empty address that is not exactly one of the platform's own storage document addresses is refused, for every visual type, with the dedicated error code VISUAL_URI_NOT_ALLOWED (numeric 12112). This means viewers' browsers are never sent to a host chosen by a member. Uploading a picture and clearing one with an empty address work as before.

## Root cause

updateVisual saved whatever address it received. Any member with UPDATE on a visual could set it to a host they control, and every viewer of that avatar or banner would then fetch from that host. Profile creation (addVisualsOnProfile) already demands an internal address for every non-avatar visual it is given, but the update path never applied that rule. This serves FR-001 to FR-007 of workspace#098: refuse any non-storage address for every visual type, use a dedicated code, check rights first, keep the empty address, leave upload and creation unchanged, and log nothing new.

## Fix

DocumentService gains isPubliclyAccessibleURL, the exact inverse of getPubliclyAccessibleURL: the documents base, one '/', and one lowercase uuid, with the pattern written out in the file. It deliberately does not reuse the isAlkemioDocumentURL prefix test, because that test accepts dot segments that resolve to the same-origin logout redirect. In VisualResolverMutations.updateVisual, after the UPDATE rights check and before the save, a non-empty address that fails this check throws a BaseException with the new status AlkemioErrorStatus.VISUAL_URI_NOT_ALLOWED. The status is registered in STATUS_METADATA as VALIDATION 112 with user message userMessages.validation.visualUriNotAllowed, and it has a 12112 row in docs/error-codes.md. The exception message carries no dynamic data, and its details hold only the visual id. The input, VisualService, the upload path and schema.graphql are unchanged.

Refs #6614. Split out of #6637, which keeps the delete-path fixes. This PR is only the one-off cleanup of the orphans those leaks left behind.

## Migration — `1790800000000-CleanUpOrphanedRecordsAndPolicies`

One-off and **reversible**. It deletes, in this order:
1. classifications, licenses and profiles that nothing names; their cascading children go with them;
2. the locations and storage buckets owned by the profiles deleted in step 1;
3. every authorization policy that nothing names, including the ones freed by steps 1–2.

Policies go last on purpose. The issue allows any order, and going last also catches the policies that steps 1–2 free.

### Backups and `down()`

Every deleted row is copied whole into `_orphan_cleanup_backup_<table>`. The copy happens in the same SQL statement as the delete, and every part of that statement reads the database as it was before any row is deleted. Three things are copied:
- the row itself;
- the children Postgres deletes with it (tagset, reference, visual, license_entitlement);
- every reference to it that Postgres sets to NULL, kept in `_orphan_cleanup_backup_nulled_references`. Today the only such reference is `file.tagsetId`.

The backups stay in place until the fix is confirmed. `down()` then inserts the rows back parents first, restores each nulled reference that is **still NULL** (one that was set since is left alone), and drops the backup tables.

The backup tables are not counted as names, otherwise the copies would keep the rows they copy. If a table is backed up but missing from `RESTORE_ORDER`, `up()` throws, so `down()` can never silently skip a backup.

**Follow-up:** once the fix is confirmed, a later migration drops the `_orphan_cleanup_backup_*` tables. Only `down()` drops them today.

### Safeguards
- **A row is kept while anything names it:** any foreign key, or any column carrying its id under the conventional name. The migration backup tables, e.g. `_auth_profile_backup_*.profileId`, hold such columns without an FK. Only an explicit list of each table's own cascading children is ignored, so an unknown reference keeps the row, including an owner whose key cascades. If nothing names a table at all, the migration throws instead of deleting every row.
- **There is no generic bucket or location sweep.** The Matrix media staging bucket is named only from configuration (`storage.file_service.matrix_media_bucket_id`). Only buckets and locations whose profile this migration deleted are removed.
- **Files are never deleted.** Their content lives in file-service storage, which only file-service may release. An unowned profile whose bucket holds files is left whole and counted in the log.
- **Rows created in the last day are skipped,** so an in-flight create, which saves children before their parent, cannot lose a child.
- **Only deleted ids come back to Node** (plus a deleted profile's location and bucket ids). Whole rows go from the delete straight into the backup inside Postgres, so ~15k policies' rule JSON is never held in Node memory.

## Dry run on a full dev copy of acceptance data (`up()` → `down()`, rolled back)

| | deleted | after `down()` |
|---|---|---|
| classifications | 2,997 | byte-identical |
| licenses / entitlements | 12 / 106 | byte-identical |
| profiles / locations / storage buckets | 44 / 44 / 44 | byte-identical |
| tagsets / references / visuals | 2,918 / 25 / 13 | byte-identical |
| authorization policies | 15,396 | byte-identical |
| files | 0 | byte-identical |

`up()` took ~14 s. A second run deletes nothing. 12 unowned profile trees whose buckets hold files are left for a file-service cleanup.

Of the deleted classifications, 729 are the live leak since April; the rest are 2025 rows whose policy was never computed, with no owner.

## Tests
- `clean-up-orphaned-records-and-policies.postgres.spec.ts` (10 cases) runs in the CI PostgreSQL job via `pnpm run test:migration:orphan-cleanup:postgres`, which fails rather than skips when `MIGRATION_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset. One case runs `up()` then `down()` and expects every table to come back byte-identical, including a nulled `file.tagsetId`. Removing any one safeguard turns a specific case red; so do dropping the nulled-reference capture and dropping the backup-table exclusion.

## Deploy notes
- Rollback: `migration:revert` restores the deleted rows from the backup tables. The deploy pipeline's gated pre-migration backup remains the last resort.
- Independent of #6637 in either order. Until #6637 ships, the delete paths keep leaking, so some orphans will reappear after this runs.

## Not in this PR
- The policy leaks of the group-A delete paths and failed creates.
- File-bearing orphan trees, historical empty orphan buckets (the 813 in the issue), and orphaned aggregators/documents: these need a file-service path.
- Dropping the backup tables (follow-up, above).

**Checks.** The image is public on ghcr.io (anonymous manifest fetch returns 200, no login needed). `docker compose -f quickstart-services.yml config` resolves. Related (remain open until manually closed): alkem-io/server#4970, alkem-io/client-web#9353.

Workspace spec: `workspace#063-callout-transfer-flow-state` — https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/feat/063-callout-transfer-flow-state/specs/063-callout-transfer-flow-state/

## What was still broken after #6339

QA re-tested #6021 after #6339 merged and acceptance criterion 3 ("same logic applies when the destination's innovation flow was changed via template", the alkem-io/client-web#9353 sequence) still failed: the transferred callout is tagged with one of the destination's **old** state names and shows on no flow tab.

## Root cause (proven at code level)

The transfer logic from #6339 is correct but validates against the destination's flow-state `TagsetTemplate` (`allowedValues` / `defaultSelectedValue`), and that template drifts from the `InnovationFlow`'s actual states through three writers:

1. **Template apply** — `updateCollaborationFromSpaceTemplate` loads the target collaboration with `calloutsSet.tagsetTemplateSet` (eager `tagsetTemplates`, `cascade: true` on every hop). `updateInnovationFlowStates` updates a *separately loaded* copy of the template and saves it; the applier's final `collaborationService.save(targetCollaboration)` then cascades the **stale** in-memory template back over the row, reverting `allowedValues`/`defaultSelectedValue` to the pre-template names. The destination's own callouts stay visible (they are re-homed by state *name*), which is why only transfers exposed it.
2. **Add / delete a single state** — neither `createStateOnInnovationFlow` nor `deleteStateOnInnovationFlow` ever rewrote the template.
3. **Rename** — `TagsetService.updateTagsetsSelectedValue` re-tagged callouts in memory on the rename branch and `continue`d without `save`; nothing cascades to those tagsets, so callouts in a renamed phase kept the old name on reload.

## Fix (behaviour-only; no DDL, no GraphQL change)

- `TemplateApplierService`: re-read the callouts set's `TagsetTemplateSet` after the flow-state update, so the cascade save persists the current vocabulary and template-added callouts are classified against it.
- `InnovationFlowService`: add/delete state rewrite the flow-state template; one shared default rule (`resolveDefaultFlowStateName`: current state while it exists, else first) now backs template apply, rename, add and delete.
- `TagsetService`: persist the re-tag on the rename branch.
- Migration `1789000000000-ResyncFlowStateTagsetTemplates` (data-only, idempotent, no-op `down`): re-derives `allowedValues` from the flow's states in flow order, repairs a missing/unknown default, and moves callout flow-state tags that match no state (case-insensitively) to that default. Existing drifted spaces (acceptance, where QA reproduced this) are healed on deploy.

## Regression tests (each RED on `develop`, GREEN here)

- `template.applier.service.spec.ts` — the #9353 sequence: the graph handed to the cascade save carries the template's new state names; template-added callouts see the updated vocabulary.
- `innovation.flow.service.spec.ts` — add-state (incl. sort-order insertion) and delete-state (incl. deleting the current state) rewrite the vocabulary with the shared default rule; two pins for the default rule on the template path.
- `tagset.service.spec.ts` — rename branch saves the re-tagged tagset.
- `src/migrations/__tests__/1789000000000-ResyncFlowStateTagsetTemplates.spec.ts` — structural pins (three ordered UPDATEs, idempotence guards, case-insensitive re-tag, no DDL, no-op down).
- #6339's transfer pins (`classification.service.spec.ts`, `callout.transfer.service.spec.ts`) unchanged and green.

## Root cause

Memo signing renders the live Yjs projection and resolves every internal image through document metadata and file-service bytes. Existing memos can still reference a document whose metadata row is absent, or whose metadata exists while the backing bytes return a typed 404. The renderer correctly fails rather than silently changing the signed output, but the existing collaboration migration worker had no memo-image discovery or repair path.

## Fix

- extends the existing one-shot collaboration migration worker with `--repair-memo-images --actor-id <uuid>`; it is a read-only dry run by default, and mutation requires explicit `--apply`
- reads each current memo through the live collaboration room, reports exact missing references and repeated occurrence counts, and only treats typed metadata absence or a typed file-service 404 as confirmed loss
- leaves authorization failures, transport failures/timeouts, 5xx responses, malformed responses, foreign-bucket metadata, and malformed internal locators untouched and reports the memo as failed
- removes only confirmed-missing image nodes from the fresh live Yjs document and persists via the existing correlated durability-barrier path, so concurrent edits are not overwritten by a stale snapshot
- preserves valid/external images and unrelated memo text, formatting, lists, and tables; rerunning a completed repair is a no-op
- reports visual loss explicitly, while the repaired projection is also the projection used by preview/signing

The memo image schema contains no alternate byte source to recover a genuinely absent internal document. Images whose metadata and non-empty file-service bytes are available are preserved.

- full `pnpm test:ci`: 793 files passed, 8 skipped; 9,247 tests passed, 28 skipped
- `pnpm build`: passed
- `pnpm lint` (TypeScript + Biome): passed

## What / why

A persona on the **generic** engine had no server-side route to receive a stored prompt graph: the invocation builder attached `promptGraph` only inside the `EXPERT` branch. So the declarative graph support merged in [virtual-contributor#122](https://github.com/alkem-io/virtual-contributor/pull/122) (conditional edges, retrieve/echo nodes, the shipped workshop payload) was live but **unreachable through configuration**.

This adds a `PROMPT_GRAPH_ENGINES` allowlist covering `expert` + `generic-openai`, new GraphQL authoring fields for the node/edge forms, an activation guide, and the workshop authoring fixture.

Closes #6385. Spec: `workspace#053-generic-prompt-graph`.

## What actually changed in production code

Most of the diff is tests and docs, but **three source files change existing behaviour** — worth reading rather than skimming:

**`ai.persona.resolver.mutations.ts` — the `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` body was restructured, not extended.** The fetch and the authorization check moved inside a `try`, an audit call was added on both the success and failure paths, and a constructor dependency was added. **The authorization check is unchanged in substance and still runs before any update**: same `grantAccessOrFail`, same `AuthorizationPrivilege.UPDATE`, same policy object, same position relative to the mutation — only its enclosing block moved. That is the property to verify when reviewing this hunk, and it is why the restructure is called out here instead of being described as an addition.

**`ai.persona.service.ts` — two conditions changed.** `input.engine === AiPersonaEngine.EXPERT` became `PROMPT_GRAPH_ENGINES.includes(input.engine)`; that is the feature. A second condition was *tightened*: `if (!invocationGraph)` became `if (!invocationGraph && input.engine === AiPersonaEngine.EXPERT)`, deliberately keeping the default-graph fallback expert-only so a generic persona with no stored graph produces **no `promptGraph` key at all** rather than inheriting expert's default.

**`prompt.graph.node.dto.ts` / `prompt.graph.edge.dto.ts` / `ai.persona.dto.update.ts`** add nullable fields; the only removal is an import line being widened.

Genuinely additive: every new test file, the docs, and the fixture. **No pre-existing test was modified or deleted** (`git diff origin/develop..HEAD -- '**/*.spec.ts' | grep -c '^-'` = 0), and the **GraphQL schema** delta is additive — 21 added, 0 breaking.

## Decisions worth reviewing

- **The story said "GENERIC"; there is no such enum value.** It is `AiPersonaEngine.GENERIC_OPENAI` (`generic-openai`) — the routing key bound to the `virtual-contributor-engine-generic` queue.
- **The allowlist deliberately excludes** `guidance`, `openai-assistant`, `libra-flow`, `community-manager`: widening requires engine-side graph execution first. A future enum value defaults to *not* attaching.
- **No validation of the graph/body-of-knowledge pairing.** `bodyOfKnowledgeID` is per-invocation from the VC, not stored on the persona, so the server cannot validate it. A retrieve-bearing graph on a BoK-less persona hard-fails at engine parse time and the member sees the standard error response — a documented precondition, not a defect.
- **No migration**: `ai_persona.promptGraph` jsonb already existed engine-independently.
- Expert behaviour is byte-identical in all three modes (stored / default / none).

## Evidence

- **Rebased 2026-10-06 onto `develop` `365de8f2b`** (was 140 commits behind). The three commits replay unchanged — the PR diff is identical to the reviewed head `e8321124` except `schema.graphql`, where develop had itself reworded an unrelated description. The old merge-from-develop commit (the only unsigned one) is gone; all three commits are signed.
- **`schema.graphql` regenerated** with `SCHEMA_BOOTSTRAP_LIGHT=1 pnpm run schema:print && pnpm run schema:sort` — output byte-identical to the rebased file. `schema:diff` against develop: **21 additive, 0 breaking**, 0 deprecated.
- Lint, typecheck, build clean. The PR's own specs: **52 / 52** across 4 files.
- Full suite **10 800 pass**. A different 3–4 tests timed out on each of two local runs under machine load average 61–184 (APM, forum sync, OIDC, auth-reset) — none touched by this PR, every one green in isolation, develop green under lighter load. **CI on this head: all 11 checks green, including the full `test` job** — the local timeouts were machine load, not the PR.
- `AiPersonaInvocationInput` remains **absent** from `schema.graphql` (count 0).
- The authoring fixture parses through the **actual merged VC engine parser** (`2920c83`): 8 nodes, 2 conditional edges, state model built. That parser is unchanged through VC **v0.4.0**, the release now going to acceptance.

## Review round (8 findings, all fixed, 0 declined)

Two independent reviewers on different providers found non-overlapping defects:

**Security** (verdict was `conditional`, now remediated):
- `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` wrote **no audit record** — a global admin could change the graph governing prompts, retrieval and member output with no attributable trace. Now audits success *and* failure with actor / persona / engine / `promptGraphChanged` only; never the graph, prompt text or credentials (SOC 2 CC7.2·CC7.3, ISO A.8.15·A.8.16). **This is what motivated the resolver restructure described above.**
- The activation guide didn't disclose that retrieve nodes send body-of-knowledge content to the **external model provider**; it now requires a data-classification check before activation.
- `edge.map` was an unbounded JSON scalar → now bounded (string→string, 100 entries, 128 chars per key/value). Structural limits only; graph semantics stay the engine's job.

**Correctness** — two of these were caught by *mutating the production code and watching the tests stay green*:
- The **round-trip test was tautological**: the mocked repository assigns by reference, so it compared an object to itself. Gutting the transformer left it passing. It now crosses the transformer/JSON seam against a separately constructed object.
- The **matrix's expert-default row** asserted only `toBeDefined()` — replacing the default graph with `{nodes:[],edges:[]}` kept it 7/7 green. It now asserts real graph content.
- **`schema.graphql` had been hand-authored**, including a *fabricated* description for the JSON scalar and wrong field ordering (~80 lines of divergence from the generator). Regenerated with the repo's own tooling and committed verbatim; this also picks up a pre-existing description drift on `develop`.

Full evidence ledger: `specs/053-generic-prompt-graph/forge-run.md` in the workspace repo.

## Root cause
`ContributorMap`'s pin popup could only render what `ContributorMapPin` carries: avatar, name and role. `ContributorCollection` built the pins from the full `ContributorCardData` and dropped every other card field. So people who share a location got less on the map than unlocated people got in the list. The inline map and the expanded-map dialog both render the same `ContributorMap`, so both had the gap. The only other consumer is the admin view-capture map in `FramingEditorConnector`, which keeps today's name-only popup.

## Fix
- **`ContributorMap`** has a new optional `renderPinCard(pinId)` slot. When the slot is set, the popup shows its content, and the map still never imports callout code. The popup:
  - is a labelled non-modal dialog (`aria-label` = the contributor's name) and gets focus when it opens;
  - closes on Esc or with a close button (reuses the existing `crd-common` `close` string, so no new i18n keys), and both return focus to the pin that opened it;
  - is capped at `min(20rem, 100vw - 2rem)` wide, which overrides maplibre's 240px `maxWidth` default;
  - is capped at `min(18rem, 60vh)` tall and scrolls inside;
  - has per-anchor offsets so it never covers the avatar, and maplibre picks the side that fits in the small h-96 map.
- **`ContributorCollection`** fills the slot with the same `ContributorCard` the list uses, built from the `filtered` data it already has (no new queries). This covers users and organisations, with Message whenever `onMessage` and `canMessage` allow it. It does this for both the inline and the expanded map. The expanded-map `DialogContent` ignores an Esc that comes from inside the popup (`onEscapeKeyDown` + `preventDefault`), so Esc closes the popup and not the whole map.
- When no slot is passed, the popup is unchanged.

### Why the Message menu works inside the popup (checked against the library source)
- maplibre attaches popups to `map.getContainer()`, but its pan/zoom/click handlers listen on `map.getCanvasContainer()` (maplibre-gl 5.24 `popup.ts` / `handler_manager.ts`). Pointer and key events inside the popup therefore never reach the map, so they can't pan it or close the popup.
- The Radix dropdown is portalled to `body` at `z-50` and mounts after the dialog, so it shows above the expanded-map dialog. Radix treats it as a nested layer, so the dialog doesn't block clicks on it.
- The popup's Esc handler ignores keys from portalled content, so Esc inside an open "…" menu closes only the menu.

## Regression test
`src/crd/components/callout/ContributorCollection/ContributorCollection.map.test.tsx` renders the real `ContributorCollection` → lazy `ContributorMap` path. Only the WebGL `react-map-gl/maplibre` layer is replaced with plain DOM stand-ins. It checks that:
- a user pin shows the full card (tagline, tags, location, role) and that Message calls `onMessage`;
- an organisation pin shows the full card (associates, website link, actions menu);
- Esc closes the popup and focus returns to the pin;
- the close button does the same;
- on the expanded map, the pin shows the full card, Esc closes only the popup, the expanded dialog stays open and focus returns to the pin.

**RED confirmed:** all 5 tests failed against unmodified `develop` (the popup had no card). I also removed the expanded-map Esc guard as a check, and the expanded-map test failed without it.

## Gates
- `pnpm vitest run`: 684 files, 5985 passed / 4 skipped
- `pnpm build`: pass
- `pnpm lint` (tsc + biome ci + eslint): pass

The new code comments carry no spec, issue or PR references.

## Not verified here
I didn't do a live browser check, since there was no running backend. A quick manual pass on mobile width and the expanded map is worth doing.

## Summary

Members can secure their account with an authenticator app, security keys and recovery codes from My Account → Security, and sign-in asks for the second factor after the password. When an organisation (or the platform) requires a second factor, covered members see a reminder with their deadline. After the deadline a refused session is routed to a 'secure your account' page with an enrol path. Organisation admins get a 'Require two-step verification for members' switch on the organisation's Settings tab, and switching it off asks for confirmation first because switching it back on starts a new fourteen-day grace.

The client-web slice of the cross-repo two-step verification feature (alkem-io/server#5913). Kratos now offers TOTP, WebAuthn security keys and lookup-secret recovery codes, and the server refuses a session that a rule covers but that did not use a second factor. ## Problem

In a direct conversation whose Matrix room is end-to-end encrypted, pressing Send shows "Send was not confirmed. Check the conversation before sending again." and no request leaves the browser.

The browser Matrix client runs without crypto. For a room that carries an `m.room.encryption` state event, matrix-js-sdk throws before making any HTTP call:

```
Error sending event Error: This room is configured to use encryption, but your client does not support encryption.
    at encryptEventIfNeeded
```

`handleSendMessage` swallows that error and returns `false`, so nothing reaches Synapse, the server logs or APM. Alkemio's own rooms are not encrypted; the affected rooms were encrypted outside Alkemio and encryption cannot be turned off again in Matrix.

## Change

## What / why

Rotates a non-refreshable Matrix credential that is 40 h old when a call click finds it due; that click opens nothing, and the call buttons return once the new session syncs. Requests no refresh token and lengthens no credential's life (workspace#102).

Synapse ends every non-refreshable session at 48 h (`session_lifetime`), which drops any call running at that moment. The refresh-token fix for minted sessions was declined (it would stretch a stolen token from 48 h to up to 30 days). This PR instead swaps a near-expiry credential at the one safe moment — before a call starts — and logs the old token out early.

- **`storage.ts` / `mintSession.ts` / `matrixCallback.ts`** — both credential writers stamp `issuedAt`; a record without it counts as due.
- **`ssoLogin.ts`** — `attemptSilentSso({ replacing })`: the record of the device being replaced is not taken as success.
- **`sessionController.ts`** — `rotateIfDue()`: one attempt per record, one rotation at a time. It takes over another tab's newer record, otherwise acquires (silent SSO, then mint; never clears storage first), then stops the old client, fires a best-effort `POST /_matrix/client/v3/logout` with the old token, and starts the new one with the chat marked as connecting. `recover()` clears the stored record only when it is the rejected device's (cross-tab).
- **`activeSession.ts`** — `rotateActiveSessionIfDue(): Promise<boolean>`.
- **`UnifiedChatPanelConnector.tsx`** — a start/join click opens the call only when nothing rotated.

## Security effect vs today

| Case | Today | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Matrix token stolen by a page script | valid ≤ 48 h | ≤ 48 h, usually ≤ 40 h (logged out at rotation) |
| Bus-minted token | ≤ 48 h per mint | unchanged |
| Stolen Alkemio session cookie | 30 d incl. chat | unchanged |
| Live devices per browser | 1 + expired leftovers | 1 (except R-RT-7) |

## What and why

Voice messages sent from Element now play inline in Alkemio chat instead of showing as a generic file chip that takes several clicks to hear.

Element sends a voice message as an `m.audio` event with the MSC3245 voice marker (`org.matrix.msc3245.voice`) and MSC1767 audio metadata (`org.matrix.msc1767.audio`: `duration`, `waveform`). The web client received these events but read none of those fields. This is **run 1** of workspace#100-chat-voice-messages: client-web playback only. Recording and sending (matrix-adapter, server, client-appstore) are deferred runs behind human gates HG-0 and HG-1.

Refs alkem-io/alkemio#2227 · workspace#100-chat-voice-messages

## Changes

- **Parse** (`matrixEvents.ts`): a private `voiceOf()` next to `positiveInt`, the single validation owner. A message is voice only when it is `m.audio` and carries the MSC3245 marker. `org.matrix.msc1767.audio` is read only when it is a plain object, because a throw would escape `refresh()` from `onTimeline` and `load()`. Duration comes from MSC1767 through `positiveInt`; waveform items must be integers in `0..1024`. Bad fields are dropped one by one and the voice player is kept.
- **Carry** (`models.ts`, `types.ts`): one optional `voice` field on the attachment.
- **Render** (`MessageAttachments.tsx`): `AttachmentVoice`, placed before the image and video branches, renders a native `<audio controls preload="none">` (operator ruling D0), 40 static bars resampled by slice peak (short waveforms stretch, long ones downsample), and an `m:ss` label when the duration is known. On failure it falls back to the existing download chip with a new voice hint, using the same condition as `AttachmentVideo` (`failed || !isHttpUrl`, then `onLoadError`). `failed` resets when the URL changes.
- **Tap guard** (`ChatThreadView.tsx`): `toggleRevealedOnTap` now ignores taps on `audio` and `video`, matching its own comment. Native media controls live in the browser's shadow root, so on touch devices every play, pause or seek used to toggle the message's time line.

Fixes alkem-io/client-web#10588

Related: alkem-io/client-web#5581 (page/journey titles; the callout dialog was outside its scope, so this is an uncovered path, not a regression)

## Root cause
`document.title` has one owner, `src/core/routing/documentTitle.ts`. It composes `${prefix}${override ?? base}`. The only writer of `base` is `usePageTitle`, and that hook is called only at page/layout level. Nothing in the callout dialog path wrote a title. When a callout detail dialog was open, including on its own `…/collaboration/<calloutNameId>` URL, the tab kept the Space/Subspace title.

## Fix
- `documentTitle.ts` gets a dialog layer: `claimDialogTitle(text)` returns a release function. The newest open claim is shown. The composition is now `${prefix}${override ?? dialogTitle ?? base}`:
  - the unread-badge `override` still wins, exactly as it wins over `base`;
  - the badge `prefix` still composes on top;
  - `base` is never overwritten, so releasing every claim shows the current page title without the page re-running its effect.
- `usePageTitle.ts`: the `<title> | Alkemio` composition (`pages.titles.separator` / `pages.titles.alkemio`) moves into `useComposedTitle`, so pages and dialogs build the string the same way. `usePageTitle` behaves the same as before (its existing tests pass unchanged).
- New `useDialogTitle(title, enabled)`. While `enabled` it holds a claim, and it releases it when `enabled` turns false or the component unmounts.
- `CalloutDetailDialogConnector` calls `useDialogTitle(callout.framing.profile.displayName, open)`. Every opener renders this connector:
  - feed card (`LazyCalloutItem`);
  - callout URL (`CrdSpaceCalloutPage` / `CrdSubspaceCalloutPage` → `CrdCalloutDialogFromUrl` → `CalloutDeeplinkView`);
  - Post Index (`CrdCalloutDialogById` → `CalloutDeeplinkView`).

  The fix is applied once, at that shared owner. The ~25 page call sites are untouched.
- `TaskBoardDialog` calls `useDialogTitle(title, open)`. A Tasks board callout does not open the detail dialog at all, from its feed card (`LazyCalloutItem`) or from its URL (`CalloutDeeplinkView`). It opens the board dialog instead, so that is the second owner. Code review found it.

### Why owned claims and not a single slot
A task's detail dialog opens on top of its board dialog (`elevated`), and both claim the title. With a single slot, closing the task cleared the title while the board was still open. Each claim now releases only itself, and releasing out of order is safe. Within one commit, React runs every passive cleanup before any setup, so swapping one dialog for another never flashes the page title.

## Regression tests
- `src/core/routing/useDialogTitle.test.ts` covers:
  - the singleton layer: dialog title shown, prefix composes, override wins, close restores base, and a base change made while open shows after close;
  - the hook: disabled does nothing; enabled → composed title; disabled or unmount → page title restored; title change followed.

  - nested claims: the board title survives the task dialog closing, and releasing out of order leaves the upper title.

  On the base code it fails, because `claimDialogTitle` / `useDialogTitle` do not exist.
- `src/main/crdPages/space/callout/CalloutDetailDialogConnector.tabTitle.test.tsx` renders the real connector:
  - closed: page title unchanged;
  - open: `Mobile issues tracker | Alkemio`;
  - rerendered closed: page title restored;
  - unread prefix composes, and unmount restores.

  Before the connector change, the open and prefix cases failed (2 of 3 red).
- `src/main/crdPages/space/callout/TaskBoardDialog.tabTitle.test.tsx` renders the real board dialog. The board title shows while it is open, the page title returns once it is closed, and the board title stays after a task dialog stacked on top of it closes. Both cases go red without the `TaskBoardDialog` change.

- `pnpm lint` (tsc + Biome + ESLint): clean (pre-existing warnings only)
- `pnpm build`: OK (first commit)
- pre-commit hook: passed

## Summary

Wherever a list of files can be added, users can now pick several files in one selection: a Documents response imports each picked document as its own staged item, the Links & Files dialogs add one row per uploaded file, and every references editor (profiles, space About and community guidelines, templates, innovation packs, posts and callouts) fills the clicked row and appends a row per further file. Up to 25 files are taken per selection; files left out by count, size or type are named in one dismissible notice, and a failed upload is reported once per file instead of one toast each. Save, Publish and template or pack actions are withheld while files are still uploading, only one pick runs at a time, and Discard or a form reset drops uploads that are still running.

## Root cause

alkem-io/client-web#10513: every file input on these surfaces accepted exactly one file per pick, so attaching several documents meant repeating the same dialog flow per file. The workspace spec workspace#094-upload-multiple-documents-files-at-once defines one selection rule, one notice and one bounded upload queue for all of them, and (story decision 10, FR-012) that the client deletes no upload.

## Fix

A shared file selection rule and notice (src/crd/lib/fileSelection, FileSelectionStatus), a silent mode on useReferenceFileUpload that rejects by type and size before any mutation and reports an uploading flag, and a row upload queue (useRowFileUploads) with one commit path for row writes (useRowsCommit), which addresses every row of ReferencesEditor and LinksPrePopulateRows by a client-only ID, so an upload result lands on its own row or nowhere. The Documents add connector imports a batch with per-item status; the Links & Files add and edit connectors use the shared upload hook, create rows under Promise.allSettled and refresh once after all settle, and a partly failed Create keeps only the failed rows, so a retry creates no link twice; LinkUrlAttachFileButton and the client-side deleteDocument cleanup are removed. Every host reads the uploading flag to withhold Save (the settings tabs through one useUploadGate helper), and the profile, About and guidelines editors are remounted on Discard so pending uploads are dropped. New strings are in the CRD namespaces in all six languages. Residual R-8 remains open: abandoned uploads, temporary from the Links & Files dialogs and permanent from a references editor on an existing entity, stay stored with their file name and uploader until alkem-io/server#6737 expires unreferenced documents; multi-file selection raises the per-pick count from 1 to 25. This is a medium residual for the release decision, not accepted by this change.

## Tests

Unit and component tests for the selection rule, the notice, the upload hook's silent mode, the row upload queue and commit path, ReferencesEditor and LinksPrePopulateRows (multi-file placement, late results, unmount, the 25-file cap, type rejections, disabled paperclips while uploading), the Documents add connector batch, the Links & Files add and edit connectors (no deleteDocument on cancel, row removal or replacement; one refresh after all rows settle; failure handling), and every host's Save withholding and Discard behaviour.

Fixes alkem-io/client-web#10443

## Summary

A collaboration-tool template whose responses are Documents now loads with the Documents response chip selected. This holds in Use template, in a phase's default template, in the template's own Edit dialog and in Duplicate. Before, these showed None. Saving a template's Edit dialog no longer rewrites the stored contribution `enabled` flag, so a template closed through the API stays closed after a metadata-only save.

## Root cause

The template reader's contribution-type table in calloutTemplateMapper.ts was written before Documents became a response type. It mapped COLLABORA_DOCUMENT to 'none', so every surface that loads a template through calloutTemplateContentToFormValues dropped the response type (FR-001, FR-002). The stored template was always correct; only the forms were wrong. Once a Documents template loads as Documents, its Edit save carries a contribution block. The shared update mapper re-derives `enabled` from the actor switches, which would reopen a template closed through the API (FR-005).

## Fix

In src/main/crdPages/templates/calloutTemplateMapper.ts: the COLLABORA_DOCUMENT row now maps to 'document', and the table's value type is narrowed to Exclude<ResponseType, 'none'>, so a 'none' row no longer compiles. calloutFormValuesToUpdateCalloutEntityInput drops the `enabled` key from the contribution block for every response type; the server's settings merge keeps an omitted field as stored. By decision, the live-post Edit dialog, Save as template and the template preview are unchanged: their reader still maps Documents to None until the shared update writer's `enabled` re-derivation is fixed separately. An open residual remains: a template created closed in the client and later switched on keeps `enabled: false` in storage. No client-web operation reads that value, and the owner decides whether it needs action.

## Tests

src/main/crdPages/templates/__tests__/calloutTemplateMapper.test.ts: the reader maps a Documents template to 'document' and keeps its actors and comments flag. A Memo case completes the six stored states (Post, Link, Whiteboard, Memo, Documents, empty). For closed templates (stored `enabled: false`; Documents with Admins, Members or None, and Links with Members), the update input's contribution block equals exactly { canAddContributions, commentsEnabled: true }, with no `enabled` and no `allowedTypes`. Both new groups failed on the previous code. test-suites RT-2 and RT-3 are un-skipped in the companion test-suites PR, which merges after this fix is deployed.

## Summary

A member now gets a security-alert email whenever two-step verification on their account changes. That covers their own change to a second factor and a support reset. The email says that two-step verification was changed and when (UTC). If the member's password no longer works, it points to "Forgot your password?" on the sign-in page. If the member did not make the change, it tells them their account may be compromised and to contact Alkemio support. It names no factor, code or device and carries no link in its body. It goes only to the address the server supplies in the event. Part of workspace#103-enable-kratos-mfa-support-totp-webauthn for alkem-io/server#5913. This service and the server deploy in either order. Until this build is live the event has no handler and no email is sent, but the server still writes its audit row. `@alkemio/notifications-lib` is unchanged: the payload type is declared in a service-side bridge file, as for the other raw security signals.

## Root cause

FR-023 of the second-factor feature requires that the member is told out of band when their second factor changes, so a takeover that adds or removes a factor does not go unnoticed. The server publishes USER_SECOND_FACTOR_CHANGE_SECURITY_SIGNAL as a raw { recipientEmail, observedAtISO8601 } body, the same shape as the password-change signal, and this service had no handler for it.

## Fix

New handler in app.controller.ts. New arms in the two event switches in notification.service.ts. Payload builder createEmailTemplatePayloadUserSecondFactorChangeSecuritySignal, email payload type and bridge type. Template user.second.factor.change.security.signal.js, on the password notice's transactional layout. The NotificationEvent enum in src/generated/alkemio-schema.ts gains UserSecondFactorChangeSecuritySignal. That one line was added by hand because codegen could not run against the server's schema at the time. The server's other schema additions for this feature, such as the second-factor settings and the admin reset mutation, are not in the generated file: this service does not use them, and the next full codegen will bring them in.

Two shared changes go beyond the new email and are worth reading at release time. (1) Settlement: the raw-recipient events now go through processRawRecipientEmailEvent, which turns the body into a payload inside the try that owns the RabbitMQ ack/nack (settleNotificationEvent). A body with no recipient is now settled instead of throwing out of the handler unacked. This changes behaviour for three existing handlers as well as the new one: USER_EMAIL_CHANGE_SECURITY_SIGNAL, USER_EMAIL_CHANGE_NEW_ADDRESS_NOTIFICATION and USER_PASSWORD_CHANGE_SECURITY_SIGNAL. (2) Addressing: for every template (all 61 address {{recipient.email}}), the recipient is now rendered without HTML escaping and handed to the mailer as a single address object instead of a string. Before, an address such as o'brien@example.org was escaped to o'brien@example.org and the mailer read it as brien@example.org. As a string, a quoted local part such as "x <victim@t.org>"@a.org would be parsed by the mailer as an address list and delivered to victim@t.org, past the blacklist, which checks the address verbatim. As an object, it is delivered to the one recipient mailbox.

Open residuals (low, not accepted). Nobody has accepted these yet. Each needs a named person's ruling and a tracking issue, and each belongs in the release risk table as open until ruled. (a) A missing or unparseable timestamp is printed as received after 'was changed on'. This is the existing behaviour of the shared formatter that the password and email-change notices use, and only a misbehaving server or a holder of broker credentials can send one. (b) If a member's address is blacklisted, the notice is dropped and the drop is logged only at verbose, which is the same as the password and email-change notices.

## Tests

notification.service.spec.ts: a raw second-factor payload, passed through normalizeRawRecipientEmailEvent and built, yields one email to the given address. The email has the required subject, the formatted time, the 'Forgot your password?' and Alkemio support sentences, and no factor, code or device wording. Bodies with no recipient on the raw security-signal events are acked or discarded rather than left unsettled. notification.templates.builder.spec.ts: each built email is composed through nodemailer, the mailer notifme's smtp provider uses, and the test asserts the envelope recipients it would deliver to. o'brien@example.org, a&b@example.org and "a b"@example.org are delivered to verbatim. "x <victim@t.org>"@a.org is delivered only to its own mailbox at a.org, never to victim@t.org. Display names are still escaped in the HTML body.

Fixes alkem-io/server#5913

## Summary

Members who enrol a second factor (TOTP, WebAuthn, recovery codes) get a login proxy that keeps counting their sign-in attempts per address: a successful password step no longer resets the per-IP counter, the counter's key comes from the edge's X-Forwarded-For rather than a header the sender sets, and a second step the proxy cannot count is refused instead of forwarded unbounded. A new in-cluster route publishes USER_SECOND_FACTOR_CHANGED when a member adds or removes a second factor in Kratos settings. Dev, test and sandbox allow 300 submissions per address, since test harnesses sign every persona in from one address.

## Root cause

With MFA enabled (alkem-io/server#5913), a password step that succeeded used to clear both counters, so an attacker holding a password could guess a second factor without bound, and the per-IP key followed True-Client-Ip / X-Real-Ip, which a sender chooses. The spec's D34, D36 and D45 require the per-IP bound to hold across both steps, and D44 requires the settings flow's factor changes to reach the notification pipeline.

## Fix

internal/clients/redis.go: ResetLoginAttempts deletes only the identifier counter. internal/webhooks/kratos-login-backoff/proxy.go: the client IP is the first valid X-Forwarded-For entry or RemoteAddr and is written to True-Client-Ip for every method; the body is read once with the decoder Kratos chooses for the Content-Type; an unreadable body is refused; when Redis cannot count, only a first step (password, passkey, oidc) is forwarded. service.go: an identifier longer than an email address can be (254 bytes) is counted per IP only, so a submission cannot write an arbitrarily large counter key. internal/webhooks/kratos-password-changed: a settings hook with ?method=totp|webauthn|lookup_secret publishes USER_SECOND_FACTOR_CHANGED with the factor named in its log lines. manifests/25 and 26 set LOGIN_BACKOFF_MAX_IP_ATTEMPTS to 300. README, openapi.yaml and apispec.yaml describe the new route and the proxy's behaviour.

## Tests

proxy_test.go covers the client-IP source, forged True-Client-Ip, Content-Type decoder choice, form and multipart parsing, an unreadable body, and refusal of an uncounted second step. service_test.go covers identifier-only reset and per-IP-only counting of an over-long identifier (which fails without the guard). second_factor_test.go covers publishing, skipping and logging for each second-factor method.

## Verification

- go test -race ./... — all packages pass
- go vet ./... — clean
- TestCheckAndIncrement_OverlongIdentifier_CountedPerIPOnly failed before the length guard ('expected no identifier key, got 1') and passes after it
- golangci-lint is not installed in this environment, so make lint could not run

## Merge order

Merges in any order against the other workspace#103 pull requests, but a merge to `develop` rolls this build to dev/test through CI: from then a successful password step no longer clears an address's counter, so set `LOGIN_BACKOFF_MAX_IP_ATTEMPTS` for those clusters first (risk R25). On every environment this build is live before that environment's Kratos values, and on production before the server release that carries workspace#103 (OG-4 (a), D40).

## Workspace feature

`workspace#103-enable-kratos-mfa-support-totp-webauthn`: [spec](https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/feat/103-enable-kratos-mfa-support-totp-webauthn/specs/103-enable-kratos-mfa-support-totp-webauthn), with its full evidence in `brokkr-run.md`.

Fixes alkem-io/server#5913

## Summary

Every OIDC login now reports how strongly the user authenticated. The access and ID tokens carry acr set to aal1 or aal2, read from the live Kratos session. A user whose session still owes a second factor (TOTP or WebAuthn) is sent back to Kratos at aal=aal2, and the pending login challenge is kept so the OIDC flow resumes after they finish it. Sometimes a remembered login's subject no longer matches the live Kratos session. Hydra now refuses that login with login_required instead of looping, and records a login.remembered_reject audit event. The event carries the Hydra subject, the live session's Kratos identity (session_identity_id), the client id and the request correlation id.

## Root cause

Enabling Kratos MFA needs the OIDC bridge to see the session's authenticator assurance level. Before this change it never set acr, and a contract test asserted acr was absent. Kratos's whoami 403 session_aal2_required had no handling, so a user who still owed a second factor could not finish signing in through OIDC. Remembered logins were accepted without checking them against the live session.

## Fix

internal/challenge/service.go reads the live Kratos session on every login acceptance. It sets acr from authenticator_assurance_level and records aal in the login context, and both consent paths copy acr into the token claims. It also refuses a remembered login whose subject does not match the session. internal/kratos/session_resolver.go maps whoami 403 session_aal2_required to a new error. internal/server/login_handler.go turns that error into a redirect to Kratos login with aal=aal2 and a return_to that keeps the login_challenge. internal/audit gains a session_identity_id field for the live session's Kratos identity. It is named to stay distinct from the Alkemio actor id. A new leaf package, internal/requestid, is now the only owner of the request correlation id: the middleware writes it and the challenge service reads it. The README and docs/operations.md describe the second-step redirect and what a rollback does to it. docs/operations.md also documents the acr claim and its lifetime: acr is fixed at sign-in and carried through refresh. A second-factor reset therefore leaves a Hydra grant held outside the application's sessions at its old acr until its refresh token expires, unless support revokes the subject's consent sessions.

## Tests

test/contract/acr_presence_test.go replaces the old acr/amr absence test. It asserts a top-level acr of aal1 or aal2 on both the ID token and the access token. internal/challenge/service_test.go covers every session error (missing, invalid, aal2 owed) on both the remembered and the fresh path and asserts the login is never accepted. It also covers refusal of a mismatched remembered login, including the audit event and its emitted session_identity_id key. internal/kratos/session_resolver_test.go covers the session_aal2_required mapping. internal/server/login_handler_test.go covers the aal=aal2 redirect and that the login_challenge is preserved.

## Verification

- go vet ./...: clean
- go test ./... -count=1: all packages pass
- Restoring the json tag actor_id fails TestResolveLoginSkipRejectsWhenSessionIdentityDiffers in both subtests; with session_identity_id it passes

## Merge order

Merges in any order. It deploys first and stays passive until Kratos offers a second factor: every whoami answers `aal1`, so nothing changes for members until the Kratos values are live (plan, *Rollout ordering* step 1).

## Workspace feature

`workspace#103-enable-kratos-mfa-support-totp-webauthn`: [spec](https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/feat/103-enable-kratos-mfa-support-totp-webauthn/specs/103-enable-kratos-mfa-support-totp-webauthn), with its full evidence in `brokkr-run.md`.

**Release order:** merge this PR, release **v0.8.28** (the tag publishes `@alkemio/matrix-adapter-lib`), and deploy that image **before** the server PR merges.

Adds the RPC topic `communication.actor.sessions.revoke` (`{actor_id}` → `{devices_revoked}`). When a user is deleted, the server uses it to delete every Matrix device of that user.

It follows the existing `communication.actor.session.create` path layer by layer:
- **DTO and topic:** in `pkg/dto`, plus the regenerated `lib/src` (`COMMUNICATION_ACTOR_SESSIONS_REVOKE`).
- **`SynapseAdmin`:** new `ListDevices` and `DeleteDevices`. All admin calls stay on `SynapseAdmin`.
- **Port method:** `MatrixPort.RevokeUserSessions` gets the user ID from IDMapper. It returns 0 without calling delete when there are no devices.
- **Service:** `ActorService.RevokeSessions` logs the actor ID and the count.
- **Handler:** `ActorHandler.HandleRevokeActorSessions`, plus its route.
- **Docs:** `MatrixAdapterProtocol_V3.md` §11b.

**Tests:**
- `TestSynapseAdmin_ListAndDeleteDevices`, which checks URL escaping
- `TestAdminAPI_RevokeUserSessions`
- `TestActorService_RevokeSessions`
- `TestHandleRevokeActorSessions`

`go test ./...` and `make lint` pass with 0 issues.

**Known limitation (low):** an actor who was never registered on Matrix gets a 404 from Synapse. The server then logs a revocation failure even though there was nothing to revoke.

## Workspace

`workspace#091-matrix-session-hardening`. The spec, plan and residual analysis are in the private agents-hq repo. Story: alkem-io/client-web#10463 (epic alkem-io/alkemio#2134).

**Why.** Matrix calls dropped about every 48 h. Synapse issued a token with a fixed expiry, and on expiry the client recovered onto a new device, which ended the call and reloaded the chats. With this feature the client renews a short-lived token in place on the same client, so a renewal never drops a call. Matrix devices are also ended when the Alkemio session ends and when the account is deleted.

**Merge order:** dev-orchestration → infrastructure-operations → matrix-adapter (then release v0.8.28 and deploy) → client-web → server.

- Unquoted configuration values beginning with a number and a size or exponent suffix, such as `0K1abc`, are now correctly parsed as strings ([#​8263](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8263), contributed by [@​koriyoshi2041](https://redirect.github.com/koriyoshi2041))
- Account JWT updates now reject invalid subject mappings instead of reporting success, and failed replacements no longer remove existing mappings ([#​8627](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8627), contributed by [@​vulragrag-star](https://redirect.github.com/vulragrag-star))
- Cached subscription results are now cleared when an already connected client sends another `CONNECT`, preventing stale results from being reused after an account change ([#​8641](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8641), reported by [@​Tan-JunWei](https://redirect.github.com/Tan-JunWei))
- Fixed several data races affecting service imports and exports during configuration reloads and account updates ([#​8675](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8675))
- Per-account routes no longer double count inbound account message and byte statistics ([#​8677](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8677))
- TLS certificate pin validation now checks the correct pins after a configuration reload ([#​8679](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8679))
- Fast batch ping no longer starts a new batch incorrectly ([#​8714](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8714))
- Auth callout rejections are now reported as authentication errors instead of account connection limit errors ([#​8688](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8688), contributed by [@​aniketatgithub](https://redirect.github.com/aniketatgithub))
- Scoped `ProxyRequired` settings are now respected in JWTs and auth callouts ([#​8694](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8694))
- Subscription interest notifications are no longer missed when a subscription is added or removed concurrently ([#​8703](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8703))
- Fixed issues with auth callout `auth_users` bypass
- Fixed a PDH counter buffer overflow on Windows

JetStream

- Stream scale-down requests are now rejected when the target replica count has no configured account tier ([#​8608](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8608))
- Stale per-message TTL entries are now removed when their messages have already been deleted, avoiding repeated expiry scans and excess CPU and memory usage ([#​8595](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8595), contributed by [@​digitalstraw](https://redirect.github.com/digitalstraw))
- The maximum deliveries exceeded advisory is now sent correctly when a consumer's `max_deliver` is lowered below a message's existing delivery count ([#​8605](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8605), contributed by [@​zeke-lin](https://redirect.github.com/zeke-lin))
- The consumer created time is now preserved after recovery ([#​8621](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8621))
- Filestore compaction now respects the configured sync settings when replacing a message block ([#​8629](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8629))
- Fixed a race during filestore compaction that could cause consumers to skip messages or lose redelivery tracking ([#​8623](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8623), contributed by [@​as-clearview](https://redirect.github.com/as-clearview))
- Concurrent updates to R1 consumers no longer lose API responses ([#​8628](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8628))
- Stream and consumer create and delete requests received during metalayer catchup now receive responses once catchup completes ([#​8643](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8643))
- R1 consumer create requests no longer lose their responses when the consumer is deleted immediately afterwards ([#​8643](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8643))
- Fixed a data race when handling consumer leader stepdown requests ([#​8647](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8647))
- Fixed a memory leak affecting pull requests and direct gets after a configuration reload when the system account is explicitly configured in the `accounts` block ([#​8650](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8650), contributed by [@​1995parham](https://redirect.github.com/1995parham))
- Fixed a panic when shutting down a clustered JetStream server immediately after startup ([#​8707](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8707), contributed by [@​clwluvw](https://redirect.github.com/clwluvw))
- Idempotent stream create requests with sources no longer time out after leader changes ([#​8703](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8703))
- Recovered ephemeral consumers with `inactive_threshold` set are now cleaned up properly after a server restart ([#​8732](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8732))

Leafnodes

- Publish permissions are now checked against the transformed subject sent over the leafnode connection, avoiding the need to also allow the original stream import subject ([#​8530](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8530), contributed by [@​fbarth-ifr](https://redirect.github.com/fbarth-ifr))
- Fixed incorrect pending byte accounting after a partial compressed write that could stall a leafnode connection and prevent it from reconnecting ([#​8636](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8636))
- Closed leafnode connections are now correctly removed from the account's leafnode list, reducing retained memory and garbage collection pressure ([#​8637](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8637))
- TLS state is now available to auth callouts when leafnodes connect over WebSockets ([#​8686](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8686), contributed by [@​jurry-duty](https://redirect.github.com/jurry-duty))
- Leafnode clients are now shed alongside regular clients during lame duck shutdown, avoiding a thundering herd ([#​8695](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8695))
- Remote proxies now support TLS with `https://` proxy URLs and an optional proxy `tls` block ([#​8701](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8701))
- Remote proxies no longer incorrectly warn that `nats://` URLs are unsupported or lose the hub's initial `INFO` message ([#​8701](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8701))
- Remote proxy options are now rejected when no proxy URL is specified ([#​8701](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8701))
- Leafnode interest and request/reply across account imports ([#​8730](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8730), contributed by [@​edjeffreys](https://redirect.github.com/edjeffreys))

Gateways

- The legacy `$GR.` reply prefix is now reserved on client ingress, preventing clients from publishing to gateway reply subjects using that prefix ([#​8615](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8615))

MQTT

- Config load no longer breaks QoS1/QoS2 delivery when `max_ack_pending` is unset ([#​8671](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8671))
- MQTT packet lengths are validated earlier against `max_payload` ([#​8692](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8692))
