### [`v1.55.0`](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/releases/tag/v1.55.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/compare/v1.54.0...v1.55.0)

#### Changelog

This is the biggest nats.go release in a long time: 47 changes with more than half of them coming from 18 external contributors - thank you all!

Most of this release is a robustness effort. Nearly 30 bug fixes address deadlocks, goroutine and timer leaks, data races and stalls in reconnect and drain handling, pull and ordered consumers, async publish and service API. It also adds the `FetchMaxBytes()` option and `Conn.RemoteAccount()`.

##### ADDED

- Core NATS:
  - `Conn.RemoteAccount()` and `ServerInfo.RemoteAccount` exposing the account the client is bound to ([#​2156](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2156))
- JetStream:
  - `FetchMaxBytes()` option to limit both the number of messages and total bytes in a single `Fetch()` request. Thanks [@​manenim](https://redirect.github.com/manenim) for the contribution ([#​2198](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2198))
  - `StreamInfo.Domain`, `StreamInfo.Alternates`, `StreamState.Lost`, `StreamSourceInfo.External` and `StreamSourceInfo.Error` in stream info ([#​2168](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2168))
  - `ErrStreamMessageExceedsMaximum` for JetStream error code 10054, returned when a message exceeds the stream's `MaxMsgSize`. Thanks [@​matehsan](https://redirect.github.com/matehsan) for the contribution ([#​2110](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2110))

##### FIXED

- Core NATS:
  - `ForceReconnect()` called while already reconnecting disabling `ReconnectWait` and custom reconnect delays, so the client dialed in a tight loop. Thanks [@​Arsen302](https://redirect.github.com/Arsen302) for the contribution and [@​MokiMeow](https://redirect.github.com/MokiMeow) for the diagnosis and test ([#​2179](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2179))
  - Connection closing for good instead of reconnecting after a partial write left a truncated message on the wire ([#​2169](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2169))
  - Connection status listeners losing an unread event and being unregistered when the next status was sent ([#​2193](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2193))
  - Message headers not counted against subscription pending byte limits, so header-heavy subscriptions could exceed the limit without reporting a slow consumer. Thanks [@​Grivn](https://redirect.github.com/Grivn) for the contribution ([#​2200](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2200))
  - Requests interrupted by a reconnect returning `ErrConnectionClosed` instead of `ErrDisconnected`. Thanks [@​AshSgDe29071999](https://redirect.github.com/AshSgDe29071999) for the contribution ([#​2129](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2129))
  - Default port added to the path instead of the host for server URLs with a path and no port, e.g. `ws://host/nats`. Thanks [@​dannyshafer](https://redirect.github.com/dannyshafer) for the contribution ([#​2177](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2177))
  - `Close()` during `Drain()` flipping the closed connection back to `DRAINING_PUBS` and flushing on it. Thanks [@​Kshot3000](https://redirect.github.com/Kshot3000) for the contribution ([#​2163](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2163))
  - `Drain()` waiting for the full `DrainTimeout` when the connection was closed mid-drain ([#​2171](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2171))
  - `IsSystemAccount()` reset to false by async INFO updates, such as cluster topology changes or lame duck mode ([#​2156](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2156))
- JetStream:
  - Pull consumer `Consume()` and `Messages()` deadlocking on `Stop()` or `Drain()` while buffered messages were still being delivered. Thanks [@​clwluvw](https://redirect.github.com/clwluvw) for the contribution ([#​2165](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2165))
  - `Messages()` iterator goroutines leaking after the connection is closed. Thanks [@​clwluvw](https://redirect.github.com/clwluvw) for the contribution ([#​2166](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2166))
  - Heartbeat timer and status listener left running when `Consume()` ends because the connection was closed. Thanks [@​clwluvw](https://redirect.github.com/clwluvw) for the contribution ([#​2164](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2164))
  - `Messages()` iterator returning `ErrMsgIteratorClosed` instead of the remaining buffered messages when `Next()` raced with `Drain()` ([#​2188](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2188))
  - Pull consumer with `StopAfter` stalling until the missed heartbeat check (30s by default) after a pull expired. Thanks [@​huynguyen7](https://redirect.github.com/huynguyen7) for the contribution ([#​2208](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2208))
  - Ordered consumer with `StopAfter` hanging on `Stop()`/`Drain()`, delivering too many or too few messages, or panicking after a consumer reset. Thanks [@​clwluvw](https://redirect.github.com/clwluvw) for the contribution ([#​2167](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2167))
  - Ordered consumer `Fetch()`, `Next()` and `FetchBytes()` blocking forever after returning `ErrOrderedConsumerConcurrentRequests`, and `FetchNoWait()` restarting from the beginning of the stream ([#​2211](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2211))
  - Ordered consumer `Consume()` and `Messages()` using the 15s pull consumer heartbeat instead of the 5s ordered default, so a stalled consumer was reset after \~30s instead of \~10s. Thanks [@​arminazimi](https://redirect.github.com/arminazimi) for the contribution ([#​2182](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2182))
  - `PublishAsync()` exceeding `WithPublishAsyncMaxPending()` under concurrent calls. Thanks [@​ShravanthReddy](https://redirect.github.com/ShravanthReddy) for the contribution ([#​2126](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2126))
  - Async publish error callbacks for messages pending during a reconnect delayed until the publisher shut down. Thanks [@​H-XX-D](https://redirect.github.com/H-XX-D) for the contribution ([#​2150](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2150))
  - Data race between `Info()` and `CachedInfo()` on streams and consumers. Thanks [@​vulragrag-star](https://redirect.github.com/vulragrag-star) for the contribution ([#​2152](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2152))
  - Reusing the same `KeyValueConfig.Sources` for several KeyValue buckets carrying the first bucket's subject transform into the next ones, so their reads returned `ErrKeyNotFound`. Thanks [@​zhechen-cs](https://redirect.github.com/zhechen-cs) for the contribution ([#​2190](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2190))
  - Object Store `GetFile()` leaving trailing bytes of an existing destination file when downloading a shorter object. Thanks [@​zhechen-cs](https://redirect.github.com/zhechen-cs) for the contribution ([#​2197](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2197))
- Legacy JetStream:
  - Async publish error callbacks for messages pending during a reconnect delayed until the publisher shut down. Thanks [@​H-XX-D](https://redirect.github.com/H-XX-D) for the contribution ([#​2150](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2150))
  - KeyValue `Create()` and `Update()` on a cross-domain mirrored bucket failing with `nats: no response from stream`. Thanks [@​spicysharkco](https://redirect.github.com/spicysharkco) for the contribution ([#​2203](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2203))
  - Object Store `GetFile()` leaving trailing bytes of an existing destination file when downloading a shorter object. Thanks [@​zhechen-cs](https://redirect.github.com/zhechen-cs) for the contribution ([#​2197](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2197))
- Service API:
  - Panic in `AddService()` on a closed connection ([#​2154](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2154))
  - Panic with `send on closed channel` when callbacks were queued during `Stop()` ([#​2173](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2173))
  - Service stopping on async errors from unrelated subscriptions with overlapping subjects. Async errors are now matched by subscription, recorded in endpoint stats and passed to `ErrorHandler`, and only a closed connection stops the service ([#​2174](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2174))
  - Stopping one service detaching the other services on the same connection from async errors and connection close ([#​2178](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2178))
  - Service and endpoint metadata changing after it was set, when the application modified the maps passed to or returned by the service ([#​2194](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2194))
  - `Reset()` clearing the endpoint queue group reported in stats ([#​2195](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2195))

### [`v2.15.3`](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/releases/tag/v2.15.3)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/compare/v2.15.2...v2.15.3)

#### Changelog

Refer to the [2.15 Upgrade Guide](https://docs.nats.io/release-notes/upgrade-to-2.15) for backwards compatibility notes with 2.14.x.

##### Go Version

- 1.27.4

##### Dependencies

- github.com/nats-io/jwt/v2 v2.8.3 ([#​8861](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8861))
- github.com/nats-io/nkeys v0.4.17 ([#​8861](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8861))
- github.com/antithesishq/antithesis-sdk-go v0.9.0-default-no-op ([#​8885](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8885))
- github.com/klauspost/compress v1.20.4 ([#​8885](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8885))
- golang.org/x/sys v0.50.0 ([#​8885](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8885))

##### Added

General

- Account subject mappings, imports, exports and leafnode remote permissions now support the `{{account-hash()}}`, `{{account-hash-import()}}` and `{{account-hash-leaf-remote()}}` subject mapping functions ([#​8670](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8670))
- TLS configuration now supports `verify: optional`, and the command line supports `--tlsverify=optional`, verifying client certificates when provided while allowing clients without certificates ([#​8812](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8812), contributed by [@​macphersonjamie](https://redirect.github.com/macphersonjamie))
- Leafnode connections now support a configurable `ping_interval` ([#​8718](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8718), contributed by [@​stackedbyaradhya](https://redirect.github.com/stackedbyaradhya))
- Gateway connections now support a configurable `ping_interval` ([#​8717](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8717), contributed by [@​stackedbyaradhya](https://redirect.github.com/stackedbyaradhya))
- The command line now supports `-t --test_reload <file>` to check whether a configuration change can be reloaded or requires a restart, returning exit code 3 when a restart is required; embedded servers can use `CheckReload` and `CheckReloadOptions` ([#​8829](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8829))

Monitoring

- Healthz now supports `leaf-remotes-connected=true`, returning an unavailable status until every enabled solicited leafnode remote is connected ([#​8735](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8735), contributed by [@​edjeffreys](https://redirect.github.com/edjeffreys))

##### Improved

General

- Route, gateway and leafnode connection logs now include remote destinations ([#​8755](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8755))
- Account import failures now log their reasons at error level ([#​8771](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8771))
- Gateway connections now validate protocol operations consistently with route connections ([#​8780](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8780))

JetStream

- Filestore subject matching and pending message calculations now avoid unnecessary scans and stop earlier when matches are found ([#​8784](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8784), [#​8803](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8803), [#​8806](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8806), [#​8808](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8808), [#​8813](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8813))
- Looking up the last sequence for a subject no longer requires loading the message, reducing work for stream operations and fast batch publishing ([#​8807](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8807))
- Filestore scans with single or multiple subject filters now avoid copying messages that do not match ([#​8854](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8854), [#​8855](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8855))
- Consumer redelivery queues no longer copy all remaining entries on each dequeue, reducing delays to delivery and acknowledgement processing with large redelivery backlogs ([#​8635](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8635), contributed by [@​as-clearview](https://redirect.github.com/as-clearview))
- Filestore scans with multiple subject filters now handle message blocks with many deleted messages more efficiently ([#​8864](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8864))
- Filestore subject scans and filtered pending-message counts now skip contiguous ranges of deleted messages ([#​8875](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8875), [#​8877](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8877))
- Loading filestore message blocks now avoids fully parsing messages when checking for `Nats-TTL` and `Nats-Schedule` headers ([#​8870](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8870), contributed by [@​adios-404](https://redirect.github.com/adios-404))

##### Fixed

General

- Lame duck mode is no longer skipped when `SIGTERM` follows `SIGUSR2` immediately, and servers continue to deliver their own replies after the lame duck event ([#​8750](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8750))
- Configuration reloads no longer disconnect clients authorized by auth callout when their permissions have not changed ([#​8759](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8759))
- Auth callout user JWT names and tags are now propagated to client information ([#​8720](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8720), contributed by [@​steve-weiland](https://redirect.github.com/steve-weiland))
- Configuration reloads now wait for server startup to finish ([#​8728](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8728), contributed by [@​edelmanjm](https://redirect.github.com/edelmanjm))
- Connz totals now correctly reflect user, MQTT client and subject filters ([#​8753](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8753), contributed by [@​NitinKumar004](https://redirect.github.com/NitinKumar004))
- Connz and Subsz pagination no longer repeats or skips entries, including connections with equal sort values ([#​8770](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8770))
- Windows PDH queries are now released if performance counter initialization fails ([#​8777](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8777), contributed by [@​cvas22](https://redirect.github.com/cvas22))
- Auth callout requests are now rejected safely when system account eventing has already shut down ([#​8804](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8804), contributed by [@​davidfarah2003](https://redirect.github.com/davidfarah2003))
- Wildcard characters inside a subject token are no longer treated as wildcard tokens or allowed to cause subject matching collisions ([#​8765](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8765))
- Account updates no longer unnecessarily recheck importers when export revocations have not changed ([#​8851](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8851))
- Configuration checks with `-t` now apply command line flags and validate options consistently with server startup ([#​8829](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8829))
- Duplicate non-queue subscriptions received over routes no longer leak interest to leafnodes and gateways ([#​8846](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8846))
- Gateway accounts in interest-only mode no longer stop receiving messages when an in-flight message races with removal of the last subscription ([#​8853](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8853), contributed by [@​paulwe](https://redirect.github.com/paulwe))
- Encrypted auth callouts are now rejected when the server has no XKey available ([#​8878](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8878))

JetStream

- Consumer info requests no longer report success for assignments that have not been committed ([#​8741](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8741))
- Push consumers with a `RateLimit` no longer stall indefinitely when a message exceeds the rate limiter burst size ([#​8748](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8748))
- Stream scale-up from R1 can now make progress under continuous writes, and scale-down no longer stalls on peers that were never added as members ([#​8762](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8762))
- Stalled stream restores now report failure through the restore completion advisory, consistently with other failed restores ([#​8691](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8691), contributed by [@​akarazhev](https://redirect.github.com/akarazhev))
- JetStream no longer shuts down prematurely during server shutdown or lame duck mode ([#​8708](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8708), contributed by [@​yousefissa](https://redirect.github.com/yousefissa))
- Raft meta-group setup failures now stop the write-ahead log instead of leaking it ([#​8722](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8722), contributed by [@​clwluvw](https://redirect.github.com/clwluvw))
- Leader transfers now retry promptly when the selected successor is slow, prefer caught-up peers and avoid persisting the same term and vote twice ([#​8751](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8751))
- Interest retention cleanup no longer purges a stream when a consumer has a zero check floor, and compaction is bounded by the stream's last sequence ([#​8757](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8757), contributed by [@​tsite](https://redirect.github.com/tsite))
- Filestore `MultiLastSeqs` no longer skips matching subjects ([#​8769](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8769))
- Fixed a directory creation race when enabling account storage concurrently with stream creation ([#​8767](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8767), contributed by [@​ansh0014](https://redirect.github.com/ansh0014))
- Deleting a stream no longer races with account directory cleanup ([#​8774](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8774), contributed by [@​ansh0014](https://redirect.github.com/ansh0014))
- Sources no longer discard the remainder of a batch when one sourced message is rejected ([#​8772](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8772))
- Pull requests made through service imports are now removed when the requester loses interest, even while response wildcard interest remains ([#​8797](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8797))
- Consumers no longer deliver while a reset is in flight or report later deliveries in reset responses, and durable mirrors and sources no longer skip messages after a reset or stale delivery ([#​8802](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8802))
- Memory store purge and last-sequence scans are now bounded by the possible sequence range ([#​8815](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8815))
- Raft health checks now wait for the leader's initial data to be applied, remain stable between heartbeats and during leader changes, and allow newly assigned replicated streams and consumers time to start ([#​8817](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8817))
- Resuming a paused consumer now wakes its delivery loop immediately, allowing pending pull requests and push deliveries to proceed ([#​8791](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8791))
- `AckAll` acknowledgements are no longer ignored after acknowledging a redelivered message ([#​8839](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8839))
- Filestore recovery failures now return the original error instead of panicking, preserve existing stream data and avoid incorrect storage accounting ([#​8844](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8844), contributed by [@​rleungx](https://redirect.github.com/rleungx))
- Streams and consumers with unsupported configuration values are now correctly marked offline, updates are rejected by meta leaders that cannot support them, and internal proposals preserve their stored configurations ([#​8843](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8843))
- Paused Raft followers can now request newer snapshots and compact their logs while catching up, preventing unbounded log growth and excessive memory use when replay resumes ([#​8842](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8842))
- Filestore recovery scans now persist per-message state indexes even if no new messages are published, and backward subject scans skip irrelevant blocks ([#​8849](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8849))
- Clustered health checks now report write errors on R1 streams ([#​8850](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8850))
- Removed peers in unmanaged Raft groups can no longer rejoin as leader ([#​8847](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8847))
- Scaling streams and consumers to or from R1 no longer loses writes or acknowledgements during the transition or violates atomic batch guarantees ([#​8766](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8766))
- Resetting consumers with the `last_per_subject` delivery policy now rebuilds the last-message-per-subject selection, preserves the correct delivery position after leader changes, and reports lookup errors instead of ignoring them ([#​8862](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8862))
- Filestore encryption key creation failures no longer leak file descriptors ([#​8873](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8873))
- The filestore access-time worker now shuts down reliably when the last store closes, preventing worker leaks or stopped timestamp updates when stores are reopened ([#​8794](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8794), contributed by [@​ajaykr0905](https://redirect.github.com/ajaykr0905))
- Rebuilding message deduplication state now skips deleted messages and expires restored entries at the end of their original duplicate window ([#​8874](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8874))
- Restoring a stream from a V2 snapshot now rebuilds message deduplication state, restoring duplicate detection and `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` checks without a server restart ([#​8871](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8871), contributed by [@​muhadyan](https://redirect.github.com/muhadyan))

Leafnodes

- Isolated spoke leafnodes no longer forward downstream leafnode interest to their hubs, and avoid collecting interest that cannot be forwarded ([#​8749](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8749))
- Leafnode interest is now withdrawn correctly when an outbound gateway connection closes ([#​8758](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8758))
- Fixed a data race when reading route leafnode origin support ([#​8779](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8779))
- Leafnode `deny_imports` no longer drops replies to hub requests, and account JWT or default permission updates no longer lose leafnode interest or reset permissions incorrectly ([#​8800](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8800))
- Leafnode connections no longer become stale when a hub sends many subscriptions during connection setup ([#​8811](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8811))
- Leafnode connections closed during acceptance are now removed from the server's connection list, preventing inflated leafnode counts and stale Leafz entries ([#​8838](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8838), contributed by [@​rnikhori](https://redirect.github.com/rnikhori))
- Enforcing account leafnode connection limits no longer risks a deadlock when processing remote connection counts ([#​8873](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8873))

Routes

- Routes without pooling now validate the route pool index correctly ([#​8782](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8782))

##### Complete Changes

#### Changelog

Refer to the [2.15 Upgrade Guide](https://docs.nats.io/release-notes/upgrade-to-2.15) for backwards compatibility notes with 2.14.x.

##### Go Version

- 1.27.3, which contains mitigations for CVE-2026-111943 by distrusting eMudhra intermediate certificates ([#​8798](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8798))

##### Dependencies

- github.com/klauspost/compress v1.20.3 ([#​8798](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8798))

##### Fixed

General

- Allowed connection types are now correctly respected in auth callout setups
- Fixed a potential queue sub weight amplification in the sublist
- OCSP responses are now correctly bound to the certificate serial number

JetStream

- Restored v1 stream snapshots now correctly guard against excessive subject lengths, subject counts or block counts

Leafnodes

- ACLs on leafnode connections no longer override allow/deny lists to implicitly allow `$MQTT.>` permissions

MQTT

- OCSP verification for MQTT connections now correctly obeys the `ocsp_peer` option in the `mqtt` block

### [`v2.15.1`](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/releases/tag/v2.15.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/compare/v2.15.0...v2.15.1)

#### Changelog

Refer to the [2.15 Upgrade Guide](https://docs.nats.io/release-notes/upgrade-to-2.15) for backwards compatibility notes with 2.14.x.

##### Go Version

- 1.27.2 ([#​8740](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8740))

##### Dependencies

- github.com/klauspost/compress v1.20.1 ([#​8737](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8737))
- github.com/nats-io/nats.go v1.53.1 ([#​8737](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8737))

##### Changed

JetStream

- The `max_ha_assets` limit is now enforced consistently by the metalayer leader during stream and consumer placement, scaling and moves ([#​8639](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8639))

Gateways

- Support for sending and handling the legacy `$GR.` reply prefix, used by servers prior to v2.1.2, has been removed ([#​8615](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8615))

##### Improved

JetStream

- Stalled source and mirror flow control is now reported in stream info and warning logs, making missing `$JS.FC.>` imports or exports easier to diagnose ([#​8633](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8633))
- Stream and consumer placement now prefers peers that have caught up with the metalayer, reducing delays in API responses ([#​8643](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8643))
- Improved the performance of deleting entries from and encoding AVL sequence sets ([#​8646](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8646))
- Fast batch publish now reports backward sequence gaps as well as forward gaps ([#​8699](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8699))
- Stream pending message calculations avoid unnecessary filestore cache access and handle deleted sequence ranges more efficiently ([#​8680](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8680), [#​8681](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8681))
- Stream restore format detection now stops after the first S2 chunk ([#​8693](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8693))
- Stream restore waits for the preferred node to become leader, avoiding an incorrect create response during clustered restore ([#​8690](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8690))
- Memory backed streams avoid copying message headers and bodies twice when storing messages ([#​8652](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8652), contributed by [@​randomizedcoder](https://redirect.github.com/randomizedcoder))

Monitoring

- Leafz now reports whether a leafnode connection uses WebSockets ([#​8683](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8683))

MQTT

- QoS2 `PUBLISH` and `PUBREL` processing is now pipelined for increased throughput ([#​8416](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8416), contributed by [@​levb](https://redirect.github.com/levb))
- Reduced allocations and buffer copying when processing QoS1 and QoS2 messages and issuing JetStream store and delete requests ([#​8624](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8624), [#​8625](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8625), contributed by [@​levb](https://redirect.github.com/levb))
- Partial packets are no longer copied in full on every read, reducing allocations and buffer copying ([#​8692](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8692))

##### Fixed

General

- `Connz` requests selecting a connection by `cid` now correctly apply account, user and MQTT client ID filters ([#​8613](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8613))
- Pipelined client operations are no longer processed after a connection is rejected for exceeding the account's `max_connections` limit ([#​8614](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8614))
- Queue subscription deny permissions are now checked against the mapped delivery subject ([#​8616](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8616))
- Outstanding reply permissions are now preserved when inherited account permissions are refreshed without changing the response policy ([#​8620](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8620), contributed by [@​0xasritha](https://redirect.github.com/0xasritha))
- Subscription deny filters are now rebuilt atomically when inherited account permissions are refreshed, preventing a window in which denied messages could be delivered ([#​8622](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8622), contributed by [@​0xasritha](https://redirect.github.com/0xasritha))
- Unquoted configuration values beginning with a number and a size or exponent suffix, such as `0K1abc`, are now correctly parsed as strings ([#​8263](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8263), contributed by [@​koriyoshi2041](https://redirect.github.com/koriyoshi2041))
- Account JWT updates now reject invalid subject mappings instead of reporting success, and failed replacements no longer remove existing mappings ([#​8627](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8627), contributed by [@​vulragrag-star](https://redirect.github.com/vulragrag-star))
- Cached subscription results are now cleared when an already connected client sends another `CONNECT`, preventing stale results from being reused after an account change ([#​8641](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8641), reported by [@​Tan-JunWei](https://redirect.github.com/Tan-JunWei))
- Fixed several data races affecting service imports and exports during configuration reloads and account updates ([#​8675](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8675))
- Per-account routes no longer double count inbound account message and byte statistics ([#​8677](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8677))
- TLS certificate pin validation now checks the correct pins after a configuration reload ([#​8679](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8679))
- Auth callout rejections are now reported as authentication errors instead of account connection limit errors ([#​8688](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8688), contributed by [@​aniketatgithub](https://redirect.github.com/aniketatgithub))
- Scoped `ProxyRequired` settings are now respected in JWTs and auth callouts ([#​8694](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8694))
- Subscription interest notifications are no longer missed when a subscription is added or removed concurrently ([#​8703](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8703))
- Fast batch ping no longer starts a new batch incorrectly ([#​8714](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8714))
- Fixed issues with auth callout `auth_users` bypass
- Fixed a PDH counter buffer overflow on Windows

JetStream

- Stale per-message TTL entries are now removed when their messages have already been deleted, avoiding repeated expiry scans and excess CPU and memory usage ([#​8595](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8595), contributed by [@​digitalstraw](https://redirect.github.com/digitalstraw))
- The maximum deliveries exceeded advisory is now sent correctly when a consumer's `max_deliver` is lowered below a message's existing delivery count ([#​8605](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8605), contributed by [@​zeke-lin](https://redirect.github.com/zeke-lin))
- The consumer created time is now preserved after recovery ([#​8621](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8621))
- Filestore compaction now respects the configured sync settings when replacing a message block ([#​8629](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8629))
- Fixed a race during filestore compaction that could cause consumers to skip messages or lose redelivery tracking ([#​8623](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8623), contributed by [@​as-clearview](https://redirect.github.com/as-clearview))
- Concurrent updates to R1 consumers no longer lose API responses ([#​8628](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8628))
- Stream and consumer create and delete requests received during metalayer catchup now receive responses once catchup completes ([#​8643](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8643))
- R1 consumer create requests no longer lose their responses when the consumer is deleted immediately afterwards ([#​8643](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8643))
- Fixed a data race when handling consumer leader stepdown requests ([#​8647](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8647))
- Clustered snapshots now use the correct generated names for ephemeral consumers, allowing backup validation and restore to succeed ([#​8651](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8651), contributed by [@​kris70lesgo](https://redirect.github.com/kris70lesgo))
- Fixed a memory leak affecting pull requests and direct gets after a configuration reload when the system account is explicitly configured in the `accounts` block ([#​8650](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8650), contributed by [@​1995parham](https://redirect.github.com/1995parham))
- Fixed membership change, learner scale-up and metalayer commit recovery issues ([#​8672](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8672))
- Fixed migration and R1 scale-up issues that could delete a running store or lose writes ([#​8673](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8673))
- Recreated streams with renamed Raft groups now start their monitors correctly ([#​8673](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8673))
- Consumers are no longer moved to new stream peers before those peers hold the stream data ([#​8678](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8678))
- Failed clustered stream restores now clean up correctly without deleting a subsequently recreated stream or losing a `stream rm` response ([#​8702](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8702))
- Fixed a panic when shutting down a clustered JetStream server immediately after startup ([#​8707](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8707), contributed by [@​clwluvw](https://redirect.github.com/clwluvw))
- Idempotent stream create requests with sources no longer time out after leader changes ([#​8703](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8703))
- Interest cleanup no longer compacts a stream past its last sequence during recovery ([#​8710](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8710), contributed by [@​pat-s](https://redirect.github.com/pat-s))
- Raft nodes will no longer leak their WAL if stopped before route connections are available ([#​8711](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8711), contributed by [@​clwluvw](https://redirect.github.com/clwluvw))
- Recovered ephemeral consumers with `inactive_threshold` set are now cleaned up properly after a server restart ([#​8732](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8732))

Leafnodes

- Publish permissions are now checked against the transformed subject sent over the leafnode connection, avoiding the need to also allow the original stream import subject ([#​8530](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8530), contributed by [@​fbarth-ifr](https://redirect.github.com/fbarth-ifr))
- Fixed incorrect pending byte accounting after a partial compressed write that could stall a leafnode connection and prevent it from reconnecting ([#​8636](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8636))
- Closed leafnode connections are now correctly removed from the account's leafnode list, reducing retained memory and garbage collection pressure ([#​8637](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8637))
- TLS state is now available to auth callouts when leafnodes connect over WebSockets ([#​8686](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8686), contributed by [@​jurry-duty](https://redirect.github.com/jurry-duty))
- Leafnode clients are now shed alongside regular clients during lame duck shutdown, avoiding a thundering herd ([#​8695](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8695))
- Remote proxies now support TLS with `https://` proxy URLs and an optional proxy `tls` block ([#​8701](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8701))
- Remote proxies no longer incorrectly warn that `nats://` URLs are unsupported or lose the hub's initial `INFO` message ([#​8701](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8701))

- Leafnode isolation is now checked before the subscription permission checks, reducing CPU usage on hubs with large numbers of isolated leafnodes ([#​8727](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8727))
- Leafnode interest and request/reply across account imports ([#​8730](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8730), contributed by [@​edjeffreys](https://redirect.github.com/edjeffreys))

Gateways

##### Go Version

- 1.27.1 ([#​8551](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8551))

##### Added

JetStream

- Desired state metalayer ([#​8432](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8432), [#​8437](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8437), [#​8439](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8439), [#​8443](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8443), [#​8452](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8452), [#​8460](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8460), [#​8476](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8476), [#​8576](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8576), [#​8598](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8598), [#​8602](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8602), [#​8603](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8603))
  - A new desired state reconciliation engine for streams and consumers considerably improves the safety and reliability of asset moves and scales
  - Updating the placement or replication factor midway through an existing scale/move operation, cancelling an in-flight scale/move, or peer-removing is now much safer
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-62.md>
- Cancel stream move endpoint ([#​8476](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8476))
  - An in-flight scale/move operation on a stream can be cancelled and the asset returned to its original placement using the new `$JS.API.STREAM.CANCEL_MOVE` endpoint
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-62.md>
- Evacuate endpoints ([#​8443](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8443))
  - The new `$JS.API.SERVER.EVACUATE` endpoint can safely evacuate streams, and any consumers on those streams, from a node
  - The new `$JS.API.STREAM.PEER.EVACUATE.*` endpoint can safely evacuate a peer, and any consumers on that peer, from a stream
  - These operations combined allow for maintenance operations with full transfer of data and state without having to peer-remove first
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-62.md>
- Metalayer rescue for disaster recovery ([#​8408](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8408))
  - The new `$JS.API.META.RESCUE` endpoint can temporarily lower the quorum-needed for the metalayer, in order to facilitate the recovery of a system where nodes have been permanently lost and the metalayer cannot reach quorum
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-61.md>
- Stream backup and restore v2 ([#​7882](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/7882), [#​8584](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8584), [#​8591](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8591), [#​8604](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8604))
  - A new backup format for stream snapshots which reads out per-message rather than per-block
  - The new backup format also now correctly includes non-replicated consumers on follower nodes
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-63.md>
- Detect source stream recreation ([#​8384](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8384))
  - The server now detects a source stream being recreated, restarting the sourcing back from the beginning, ensuring new messages are sourced
- Stream source indexing ([#​8282](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8282), [#​8516](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8516), [#​8283](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8283))
  - Restarts and leader changes previously required expensive backward scans through the stream to find the last sourced indices. These are now persisted in an index for instant lookup.
- Domain-prefixed JS API in system account ([#​8429](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8429))
  - When a system account is bridged between the hub and a leaf node, the domain-prefixed JS API can now be used to operate on the leaf node while directly connected to the hub

##### Changed

JetStream

- Streams now have a default limit of 1000 consumers, unless `max_consumers` is specified in the stream config or account limits ([#​8337](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8337), [#​8566](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8566))
  - Applications planning to use a large number of consumers on a stream should configure `max_consumers` in the stream config or account limits to an appropriately high number
  - The server-wide default of 1000 can be overridden by setting `default_max_consumers` in the JetStream limits, or can be disabled by setting to `-1`
  - This limit does not affect existing consumers and will not result in consumer deletions, only the creation of new consumers is prevented
- Sync changes for replicated streams ([#​8447](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8447))
  - When the `sync_interval` is set to `always`, replicated streams now sync their WAL entries but no longer sync upper stream layer writes
  - The synced log allows the stream to recover safely, but removing unnecessary syncs from the upper stream layer dramatically improves performance
  - Non-replicated R1 streams are not affected by this change and will continue to sync at the stream layer as normal
- The `js_raft_delete_range` feature is now enabled by default ([#​8520](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8520))

Leafnodes

- The `no_advertise` option no longer includes the hub's own listener address ([#​8451](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8451), contributed by [@​freakes](https://redirect.github.com/freakes))

##### Improved

JetStream

- Shorter wait for durable source/mirror consumer resets ([#​8323](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8323))
  - When using durable consumers for sourcing or mirroring, the heartbeats now short-circuit the recreation backoff
- An atomic batch for a single-replica stream run with `sync: always` now syncs messages as a group ([#​8539](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8539), contributed by [@​RainyPixel](https://redirect.github.com/RainyPixel))
- JetStream source/mirror reply subjects can now opt-in to be domain/account aware ([#​8586](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8586), contributed by [@​ayushk-1801](https://redirect.github.com/ayushk-1801))

MQTT

- QOS 1 published into JetStream are pipelined for increased throughput ([#​8415](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8415), contributed by [@​levb](https://redirect.github.com/levb))

##### Fixed

Leafnodes

- Leafnode isolation using `request_isolation`, or with hub-enforced `isolate`, now works correctly across cluster nodes ([#​8504](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8504))

The next release in one PR. It brings two features to `develop`. Each one's spec, plan, contracts and tasks are in `specs/`.

| Feature | What it does | Details |
|---|---|---|
| **026 — Space access gate** | Use of an app depends on the person's **role** on designated Alkemio Spaces. Production gates only the VNG monitor, by [`programmagroei`](https://alkem.io/programmagroei) | `specs/026-space-access-gate/`, previously #164 |
| **027 — VNG admin area** | The monitor gets its own list of Spaces, a settings area for managers, and no Space selection for viewers | `specs/027-vng-admin-area/`, previously #168 |

> 027 builds on 026 and **changes one of its rules**. **Manage** is now `ADMIN` on one of the app's separate **admin Spaces** (`access.vng_admin`, default `programmagroei`), even without `MEMBER`. 026's "MEMBER + ADMIN on the same Space" rule is gone.

## What changes for people

- **Signed out:** the sign-in screen lists the Spaces whose members can use the monitor, with links.
- **No access:** a no-access screen lists those Spaces, with **Opnieuw controleren**. "Could not verify" (Alkemio slow or unreachable) is a separate screen; it fails closed and is never held. A refusal mid-session switches to it, with no toast and no sign-in loop.
- **Viewers (VNG):**
  - No Space selection: no selection column or drawer, no hub picker, no narrowing. The monitor always reports on the Spaces its managers chose.
  - Header:
    - **In deze monitor** opens a list of those Spaces. It flags any Space missing from your own data (usually: no read rights) and says who has access.
    - **GemeenteDelers meenemen** is a switch that shows a count when it is on.
    - Refresh.
  - The yellow banner stays and now also says which Spaces' members have access. The user menu shows your role ("Gebruiker" or "Beheerder van de monitor") and the same Spaces.
- **Monitor managers:** a settings button opens `/admin`, over the dashboard, so coming back keeps your tab and data. It has four sections:
  - who can use the monitor;
  - **Spaces in the monitor**: view and edit, with a pending diff and a "someone else saved" dialog; additions are limited to top-level Spaces you can read;
  - **classifications of one initiative**, written to Alkemio when you may update that Space;
  - the **GemeenteDelers source**.
- **Explorer and GovTech:** explicitly ungated, with unchanged behaviour. GovTech keeps hub selection.
- **Dutch copy:** "je", "Space", "Inloggen/Uitloggen".

## How it works

- **One access module, `server/src/access/`**
  - Every app must declare `access.<app>`: its viewer Spaces, or `none`. A missing or invalid value stops start-up.
  - **Roles, not privileges.** READ on a public Space is granted to everyone.
  - Enforced before every router with a 403 `ACCESS_DENIED`, distinct from 401. A request belongs to its listener's app **plus any app it names**, which closes the path to `/api/vng/*` through the Explorer's port.
  - The decision is made once per session per app (`access_decisions`, keyed by both Space sets). `requireAccess({ fresh: true })` re-checks with Alkemio before every admin write.
  - New public endpoint `GET /api/auth/access/spaces`. `/me` returns `access.viewerSpaces`.
- **Monitor settings, `server/src/settings/`**
  - Their own tables in the existing single SQLite file. Cache operations never touch them.
  - Seeded once from `monitor-settings.seed.json`, which equals today's `vih-test` hub (23 Spaces).
  - Saves carry a revision (a stale save gets 409). Change history is append-only.
  - A daily backup copies only the settings tables, and `node dist/settings/restore-cli.js` restores them.
- **Scope and admin API**
  - VNG reads `GET /api/vng/scope` (SQLite only) instead of a hub.
  - `/api/vng/admin/*` runs with the manager's own token. It includes the first mutation document in the repo, `UpdateClassificationSelection`.
- **Database:** new tables `access_decisions`, `settings_meta`, `settings_state`, `included_spaces`, `settings_changes`, `classification_changes`. No `CACHE_MAINTENANCE_VERSION` bump.
- **Constitution:** 4.3.2.
- **New configuration:**
  - `VNG_ADMIN_GATE`, `VNG_ACCESS_GATE_NAMES`, `SETTINGS_BACKUP_DIR`, `SETTINGS_BACKUP_KEEP`.
  - `VNG_ACCESS_GATE=none` now also needs `VNG_ADMIN_GATE=` (empty).
- **Dev:** each SPA proxies to its own listener: VNG on :4101, GovTech on :4102.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- **Operational guarantees, handled separately:** a persistent volume, a backup location that survives losing it, and a restore drill.
- **Accessibility follow-up:** keyboard navigation inside the popovers, and real modal dialogs in the admin area. The easy fixes are included.
- **Known, unrelated failure:** `tests/vng-initiatives-export.spec.mjs` header test already fails on `develop`. It expects no Groeifase/TRL columns.

## Test plan

- [x] Server: 489 tests, `tsc` clean. Covers:
  - the policy and sets logic, the per-Space checks, the probe and the decision store;
  - real-HTTP gating, including the Explorer-port path, and 401/403 on every admin route;
  - the settings store, seed, backup/restore and isolation from the cache;
  - GemeenteDelers counts matching the browser summary.
- [x] VNG unit tests (199). Builds pass for VNG, GovTech and Explorer.
- [x] Playwright VNG specs: 61, including `vng-access-gate`, `vng-admin-area`, and `mobile-navigation` at 390, 820 and 1440 px.
- [x] Built server against a temporary DB: seeds 23 Spaces and writes a backup. A second start doesn't re-seed, and the restore CLI works.
- [ ] End-to-end sign-in with a real member and a real non-member account (026 quickstart §3).
- [ ] T058: confirm with two accounts that `UPDATE` on `about.authorization.myPrivileges` predicts whether a classification save succeeds.
- [ ] T070: the 027 manual scenario run (quickstart §3).

## Summary

The Playwright nightly of 16 Nov ([run 43894982021](https://github.com/alkem-io/test-suites/actions/runs/43894982021)) had 7 failed tests. Some of the 26 tests that did not run sit behind them, in the same files; I did not count how many. None is a product defect. Five are specs that a client-web change left behind, and two are a set-up that trips a rate limit on the test cluster. This PR fixes all seven in the tests. No test is skipped or removed.

## Causes and fixes

| Tests | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Chat avatars US1-AS1, US3-AS1 (and the rest of both files, which did not run) | The test cluster limits `/oauth2/auth` to 30 requests a minute per source address, burst 10 (Traefik middleware `hydra-authorize-rate-limit`). A sign-in passes through it three times and the chat's silent sign-on three more. `registerAndSignInAll` signed three people in at once, so it spent 18 and got HTTP 429. The browser stayed on the refusal and the set-up timed out. | Sign-ins queue, one at a time. A refused sign-in reloads the refusal, whose verifier is unspent, and carries on. Each sign-in waits for the page's first Matrix sync before the next starts. |
| Chat avatars US1-AS7 | client-web#10583 shows a message's time as a tooltip on the bubble. The spec still looked for a timestamp line in the message column. | The timestamp check is removed; the reaction checks stay. |
| Organization user associates US1-AS2; Organization email invitations US1-AS2 and US2-AS6 (and the chained cases behind them) | client-web#10499 renamed the bin button on a pending row from "Delete" to "Revoke invitation". | The specs use the new name. The confirmation dialog's button has the same name, so the confirm click is scoped to the `alertdialog`. |
| Comment images US1-AS2, US1-AS8 | client-web#10510 opens a comment's picture in a viewer over the thread. The specs waited two minutes, three times, for a new tab. | The specs check the viewer shows the picture, that it loaded, and that its address serves `image/png` from storage. |

The same rate limit explains the Chat avatars failures of the 13 Nov run ("Send was not confirmed", a message that never showed): when only the silent sign-on was refused, the chat session came up late.

## Verification

- **Chat avatars:** run against `test-alkem.io` from a laptop. Before the fix the trace shows the 429 on `/oauth2/auth` and the stuck sign-in. After it, the whole project made 42 requests to `/oauth2/auth` with no refusal, and every test body passed except US1-AS7, which failed on the timestamp line this PR then removed. US1-AS7 was not run again after that removal. The files' teardown could not run there, because the laptop does not have the test environment's harness password.
- **Organization suites and Comment images:** not run. They seed through the admin persona, which needs that password. The new locators were checked against client-web `develop`: `PendingMembershipsTable` and its test for the button name, `ConfirmationDialog` for the `alertdialog` role, and `MessageAttachments` with its test for the viewer's name, image and Close button.
- ESLint and `tsc --noEmit` pass on the changed files.

The next nightly is the first full run of these fixes.

## Follow-up, not in this PR

The `/oauth2/auth` limit is per source address, so it caps the whole run at about five browser sign-ins a minute. That matters for running the nightly with more than one worker. Raising the limit for the test cluster is a `dev-orchestration` change.

## Summary
When Swarmail is the mail sink, the notification test helpers wait for mail through Swarmail's event-driven `await` endpoint instead of polling the MailSlurper API and sleeping fixed delays. Without Swarmail nothing changes: the helpers poll `MAIL_SLURPER_ENDPOINT` exactly as today.

This follows the switch of dev and test to Swarmail (alkem-io/dev-orchestration#117).

## Changes
- **`notification.helpers.ts`** (only when `SWARMAIL_API_ENDPOINT` is set):
  - waits go to `GET /api/v1/inboxes/default/await?count=N&timeout_ms=…`, in 5 s slices (`SWARMAIL_AWAIT_SLICE_MS`), so a wipe in the middle of a wait is noticed;
  - the settle delays drop to 1 s;
  - negative checks ("no mail is sent") keep their full quiet window;
  - polling stays as the fallback.
- **`nightly-build-trigger.yml`:** the test step passes `vars.SWARMAIL_API_ENDPOINT` through, for example `https://test-alkem.io/swarmail-api`. That is Swarmail's read-only inbox route from alkem-io/dev-orchestration#117: `GET` under `/api/v1/inboxes` only. No port-forward is needed. When the variable is empty, the suite polls.

## Evidence
Swarmail trial on the test cluster, notification suite without `messaging/` (alkem-io/test-suites runs 42327018660, 42329811921 and 42332295821):

| Sink | Passed / failed | Test time |
|---|---|---|
| MailSlurper | 191 / 5 | 1305 s |
| Swarmail, polling | 192 / 4 | 1217 s |
| Swarmail, these event-driven waits | 192 / 4 | **1116 s (−14.5%)** |

The same 4 tests fail with every sink: push and reaction-window checks, not mail. The largest per-file gains were `associates` (91 s → 48 s), `form-response` (39 s → 26 s) and `post-contribution` (83 s → 67 s).

The nightly project only touches these helpers in a few files, so expect little change there. The gain shows up when the notifications project runs.

## Safe to merge before or after the switch
The helpers act only when `SWARMAIL_API_ENDPOINT` is set, and the repository variable is set only once test runs Swarmail with that route. Merging this first changes nothing.

## What

`ensureAuthorizationPolicies` — a new lib step wired into server-api global setup after `ensureHarnessAdminRoles` — issues `authorizationPolicyResetAll` as the harness admin, waits for the server's asynchronous reset task, then for a space read to settle. Governed by `AUTH_POLICY_RESET_ON_SETUP`:

| value | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `off` (default) | never resets — nothing changes for the nightly |
| `always` | resets unconditionally, e.g. right after a server upgrade that changed authorization rules |
| `auto` | resets only when the admin is denied a space read |

`AUTH_POLICY_RESET_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 300 s) bounds the wait. The step runs after the role grant on purpose: a bootstrap admin without `PLATFORM_CONTENT_FULL_ACCESS` is denied `Space.settings` for want of the role, not of a reset.

## Why

A server upgrade that changes the authorization rule set leaves every stored policy as it was until the reset rewrites it. Until now that was a manual mutation someone had to remember (the server's `dev-seed-roles` compose service prints it as its last line). With this it is one env var.

## Verification

- Live on a locally seeded stack (server 0.171.0): `auto` detected the denied read, issued the reset, the task completed 61/61 while the auth-reset worker scaled 0→3→0, and the settle window then correctly reported the admin still denied — because it lacked the content role, which `ensureHarnessAdminRoles` grants. That finding is why the default is `off` and the probe runs after the grant; it is recorded in `docs/qa-knowledge/harness.md` together with the seeded-admin vs harness password split that actually blocks local runs.
- `off` verified as a no-op.
- `pnpm -C lib run lint` (0 errors, pre-existing warnings only), `pnpm -C lib run build`, server-api `tsc --noEmit` clean.

- `lib/src/scenario/registration/ensure-authorization-policies.ts` (new) + barrel export
- `lib/src/config/alkemio-test-config.ts`, `create-config-using-envvars.ts` — `authorizationReset { mode, timeoutMs }`

## What

The **W1 server behaviour knowledge base** for the rebuild: 34 tables of behaviour rules under `docs/qa/server-rebuild/knowledge/`, plus the generated access matrix. Together they state what today's server guarantees, why, for whom, and how much of it is proven — the oracle the new core is checked against and the gaps list the new net is built from.

Docs only. Base `develop`. Ten signed commits.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tables | 34 — 23 of the 25 legacy test areas (`platform-roles` and `storage` are collapsed into the access matrix) + 11 catalogue features with no legacy test folder |
| Rules | 1,119 |
| Findings (sources disagree or likely defect) | 322 |
| Access matrix | 237 resources × 42 roles × 18 settings variants; 2,631 legacy cases mapped to cells, 11 cross-check findings |
| Server | `develop` @ `eeecf9ddb` (Release/79; authorization builders identical to `v0.170.2` on acceptance) |

## Method — three sources per area

Each table is drawn from three sources with different jobs, so a table cannot inherit a hole the legacy suite had:

1. **Server code + GraphQL schema** give the universe of behaviours (enums, seeds, rules, builders).
2. **The legacy server-api suite** gives the proof: a rule with a green case is *proven*; a rule the code states and no case asserts is *untested* and goes to the gaps.
3. **Specs, ADRs and issues** give the why. Where none exists the row is *unknown-why* and a person fills it.

Where the three disagree the disagreement is a numbered **finding**, never resolved towards the code. Every table has a **who-may** role × action block drawn from the matrix, a constants table with a "product must rule?" column (the rebaseline candidates), the untested rules as its gaps list, and an **open questions** section for what the sources could not settle. The headline findings of every table were spot-checked against the server code; the few claims that could not be located by name are marked as such in the tracker rows.

The first table was extracted from the tests alone and carried 6 of 16 entitlement types, 2 of 11 plans and 2 of 4 feature roles; the method change (`plan.md` § W1) came from that.

## Files

- `knowledge/<area>.md` × 34 — one per area or catalogue feature. Each opens with a one-line **review load** (findings · unknown-why · untested · constants · open questions).
- `knowledge/REVIEW-GUIDE.md` — the seven steps the signing person does with a table; the five places that carry their signature.
- `knowledge/access-matrix.md` + `.json`, `access-matrix-crosscheck.md` + `.json`, `_tools/access/` — the generated oracle, its cross-check against acceptance data and the two largest suites, and the generator.
- `plan.md` § W1 — goal, status values, the three-source method, the who-may block.
- `README.md` (tracker) — W1 progress by area and by catalogue feature, open items, log.

## What to look at first

One ruling closes several tables where noted.

- **Any visitor can read any account's licence, limits, usage and hosted resources** (entitlements F-5, account F-1, innovation-pack F-2).
- **F1 — every document in a space's direct storage bucket is readable without signing in**, whatever the privacy (access matrix; 296 files on acceptance).
- **Push subscriptions accept and POST to any endpoint**, internal addresses included; re-subscribing re-binds an endpoint to another user (push-notifications).
- **Renaming an innovation-flow state sets the callout re-tag in memory and skips the save** (innovation-flow; needs a live probe).
- **Summoning a virtual contributor in a room has no authorization call** (vc-knowledge-base).
- **The `task`/`tasks` queries carry no guard** (admin-operations).
- **A private space's community guidelines are world-readable** by unconditional grant (community-guidelines).
- **`transferVirtualContributorToAccount` is declared as returning `InnovationPack!`** (account).
- **Search returns private top-level spaces to everyone** by design comment; `last` pagination without a cursor returns the first page (search, pagination).
- **Organisations are created with no owner; `requiresEntryRole` is enforced nowhere** (contributor-management, roleset).
- **The room row is removed before the Matrix delete; nobody holds DELETE on a conversation** (communications).
- **The free tier is never issued; the plus trial's expiry is never evaluated** (entitlements).

## How this is reviewed

Per `knowledge/REVIEW-GUIDE.md`: the QA lead signs the why column, decides each finding (file / record as rule / drop), ticks the constants product must rule on, and answers or routes the open questions. Then one product/CTO pass over all findings and ticked constants, and the ticked rows become the rebaseline register (W1 output a). The tracker's open item 3 carries this.

## Not done / caveats

- Nothing is signed by the lead yet; nothing was filed in GitHub; no database was written.
- Three claims could not be located by name and are marked in their tracker rows: the callout post-created push ordering, the collabora rename validator, the `platform.settings` guard. Two more rest on an open issue rather than a line: the template memo with no owner (server#6682), the guest-enabled whiteboard ignoring privacy.
- Sibling clones used for context are behind: notifications (2026-08-05), matrix-adapter (2026-07-21), the engines (2026-07/08); `assistant-service` and `wopi-service` are not local. Each table's open questions say so.
- Several workspace specs exist only on `agents-hq@origin/main`; citations carry that prefix until the local clone is pulled.
- Data-dependent matrix cells are modelled on one representative and marked `data-dependent` in the JSON.

Durable Playwright cover for **workspace#051-cleverbase-account-linking** — the Connected Accounts section on Security settings, shipped in alkem-io/client-web#10176 (merged to `develop` 2026-08-24).

The forge run's Phase-V acceptance walks were driven ad-hoc and **persisted no specs** — its own ledger recorded *"Emitted @forge-acceptance specs: none persisted … the durable-spec follow-up can ride the test-suites flow."* This is that follow-up.

## Coverage — 13 cases, 7 files

`client-web/src/functional-e2e/connected-accounts/`

| Case | What it pins |
|---|---|
| CA-01 | three provider rows *Not connected* + Connect, read-only credential rows, no identity leakage |
| CA-02 | credential rows route via in-page anchors to the password/passkey cards, no inline mutation |
| CA-05 | a password error stays inside the password card (does not echo into the section) |
| CA-06 | owner-only: a platform admin on another user's security URL is redirected, no settings flow created |
| CA-04 | fail-closed when the settings flow is unreadable — explicit error + retry, **zero** provider rows; retry recovers in place |
| CA-03 / CA-07 | last-method lock shows a focusable `aria-disabled` Disconnect carrying its reason; curing the lock flips the same row to enabled |
| CA-30 / CA-31 | disconnect requires the confirm dialog — confirming POSTs `unlink=<provider>` with zero provider contact, Cancel fires no POST |
| CA-20 / CA-21 | Connect natively POSTs `link=<provider>` + CSRF to the flow action and writes the outcome marker; returning from an interrupted Connect announces the retry notice once |
| CA-40 / CA-42 / CA-43 / CA-43b | errored-flow resume (`4000007`) on bare `/settings`, and each outcome announcement — pending, connected, disconnected — exactly once |
| CA-41 | regression: the recovery-born settings flow still renders *Set new password* on bare `/settings` (the T027 resume seam) |

Live dev stack throughout; Kratos settings-flow **reads** are mocked only where a state cannot be provoked deterministically (locked rows, unreadable flow, completed round-trips). All URLs resolve at runtime from each persona's own profile URL — never a hardcoded `/user/<slug>`.

## Harness changes these depend on

- **`authenticated-session.fixture.ts`** — persona sessions are validated against Kratos `whoami` before reuse, and gain `maxSessionAgeSeconds`. Kratos gates privileged self-service operations behind `privileged_session_max_age` (15m); a live-but-stale cached session makes a privileged submit redirect to a re-auth screen instead of returning the expected settings-flow response. Specs doing privileged work now re-mint rather than mis-assert.
- **`config/global-setup.ts`** — provision personas through the Kratos **admin** API when `KRATOS_ADMIN_URL` is reachable (deterministic; no HIBP/self-service policy; a reset Kratos store heals on the next run instead of timing out every login), falling back to self-service registration otherwise. Then warm every persona's storage state **serially, before any worker exists** — concurrent cold logins were blowing the 30s budget as `Test timeout … exceeded while setting up storageState`. Warm-up failures are deliberately non-fatal so only the affected specs go red, attributably.
- **`getRecoveryLink(recipientEmail?)`** — the MailSlurper inbox is shared. An unfiltered subject match could open **another suite's** recovery mail and complete recovery against it, silently resetting that persona's harness credential for the rest of the run. `authentication-password-recovery.spec.ts` updated to pass its own address.

## Gates

- `tsc --noEmit` clean — `client-web` and `lib`
- `eslint` clean on every new/changed file
- Commit GPG-signed

## Run results — 15 / 16 green

Run against the local dev stack (client-web on `develop` incl. the merged #10176; Traefik origin `:3000`), `KRATOS_ADMIN_URL` set so `global-setup` provisions personas through the Kratos admin API.

| Run | Workers | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 15 passed, 1 failed (3.1m) |
| 2 | 2 | 15 passed, 1 failed (1.9m) |
| 3 | 1 | 15 passed, 1 failed (2.2m) |

The 15 are stable and fast (1.5-4.7s each) across all three runs — every case that exercises Connected Accounts itself is green.

### The one failure is NOT a test defect and NOT 051

**CA-41** times out at its first UI step, waiting for `Forgot password?`, with the login page frozen on *"Preparing secure sign-in…"*. Root cause reproduced with **zero test code involved** — a bare fresh browser context hitting `/login` directly:

```
401 /api/auth/oidc/id-token-hint | 302 /api/auth/oidc/login | 302 /oidc/login
303 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser
200 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser     <-- flow created TWICE
403 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/flows?id=...
{"error":{"id":"security_csrf_violation","code":403, ...}}
```

Two defects, both on the **login/OIDC bootstrap** — a surface 051 does not touch:

1. The login flow is created **twice** in one cold sign-in; the SPA then fetches the flow id from the URL while the anti-CSRF cookie has moved on, and Kratos rejects it with `security_csrf_violation`.
2. On that 403 the SPA **hangs indefinitely** on "Preparing secure sign-in…" — no error surfaced, no retry, no recovery.

Reproduction rate on this stack was high but not total (one fresh context in an early batch of three succeeded; a later batch of four failed 4/4), which is what made CA-41 look flaky before the cause was isolated.

This is the same *class* of bug the 051 review already fixed on the settings page ("settings flow created before `profileUrl` resolved — double flow creation, lost `return_to`"); this is the login page's version of it, and it is pre-existing.

**CA-41 is a regression guard for pre-existing recovery behaviour**, so it never reaches the 051 code under test. It should not gate this PR's assessment of the feature, but it does need a decision: fix the login bootstrap, or make CA-41 tolerate a stale flow id.

### Still manual

The 8 off-site OAuth round-trips (LinkedIn/Microsoft/GitHub) from the original walk stay out of automation; the provider hop is asserted up to the redirect only.

Runs the nightly `server-api` suite in parallel — **79.2 min → 44.5 min (~1.8×)**, measured on `test-alkem.io` — without weakening a single assertion. All 108 files still run; nothing is skipped,
  deleted or quarantined to gain speed.

  `workspace#040-parallel-nightly-server-api` · story #570

  ## How it works

  The 108-file `nightly` project becomes two projects in the **same** config, run as **one** invocation: `nightly-parallel` (94 files, `groupOrder: 0`, `maxWorkers` from `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS`) and
  `nightly-serial` (14 files, `groupOrder: 1`, `maxWorkers: 1`). Sequential groups give lane separation without a second config or a report merge. The legacy `nightly` project is left **byte-untouched**
  as the rollback surface — reverting is one line in `package.json`.

  Lane membership is **derived, never hand-maintained**: a guard applies hazard rules with name-scoped transitive taint, proves the two lanes partition the nightly scope exactly, and fails closed on
  drift. New spec files default to serial until proven safe — which is how two specs that arrived from `develop` mid-flight were classified with no manual step.

  Three mechanisms protect the signal: **serial-confirm** (any parallel failure is re-run at one worker, and the *serial* verdict is the job's exit code; parallel-fail/serial-pass is logged as
  interference and demotes a file after ≥2 in 7 nights), the **lane guard**, and a **retrospective baseline diff**.

  ## The main finding

  Four static-analysis passes added rules and demoted 22 files, and each run still found interference the rules missed. Two runs on identically fresh databases gave **7 and 63 failures** — same code, same
  data. Every one adjudicated as interference, never a real defect.

  The hazardous pattern is *"assert a shared pool user's privileged action succeeds"* — most of the suite, and not soundly detectable statically. The server compounds it: the `ActorContext` cache is keyed
  by actor alone and **deleted** on any credential change for that actor anywhere.

  So the sharing was removed. **Each vitest worker now gets its own 13 identities** (slot from `VITEST_POOL_ID`; worker 0 keeps bare addresses, worker N uses plus-addressing). Under `pool: 'threads'` a
  worker runs one file at a time, so two concurrently-executing files **cannot** resolve the same identity — structural, not heuristic. On `test-alkem.io` a full run then came back **`exit=0`, 108/108 
  files, 2003 passed, zero failures**.

  This needed a non-obvious fix: `GLOBAL_ADMIN` is granted by the server's bootstrap against the literal `admin@alkem.io`, so per-worker admins were unprivileged and every global-admin scenario failed
  `FORBIDDEN_POLICY`. The harness now grants platform roles per slot at startup using worker 0's bootstrap-privileged token.

  ## Teardown was silently broken

  `cleanUpBaseScenario` wrapped its whole delete sequence in **one** `try`, so the first failure skipped every delete after it. And `deleteOrganization` fails while the account still hosts anything — with
  the org **last**, that failure was invisible. An organisation leaked on essentially every run, of every suite using the factory.

  Measured: wall-clock rose **20.5 → 28.7 min across six consecutive runs**, then dropped straight back to 21.1 when the database was recreated. **~36% of runtime was accumulated residue** — larger than
  every optimisation here combined.

  Teardown is now per-entity best-effort and enumerates what the account still hosts, deleting in the required order (L2 → L1 → L0 → VCs → packs → org). Verified behaviourally: the organisation is
  genuinely gone afterwards, including when an untracked resource was created under its account.

  ## Also here

  - **`uploads.it-spec.ts` is green** — long red because an organisation profile's first visual is an AVATAR, aspect-ratio-locked to 1:1, and the fixture was 410×256. The server was right; the fixture was
  stale.
  - **Environment allowlist guard** — refuses to provision identities against an unapproved host. The Kratos *admin* path bypasses the mail-verification step assumed to protect acc/prod, and this branch
  grows the pool to 13×W accounts with programmatic `GLOBAL_ADMIN`.
  - **Playwright traces no longer published publicly** — one published trace held 73 `ory_kratos_session` entries. They now go to a private 14-day artifact; screenshots and the summary still publish.
  - **Fail-loud worker sizing** — an oversized `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS` aborts naming the variable instead of silently halving the run and reporting green.
  - **Honest mint gate** — it had come to derive its expectation from the code path it polices; now also asserts an independent ceiling, so a duplicate mint can't hide.
  - **Skips never fail the build** — skipped/todo were recorded as failures, so ~59 phantom regressions would have appeared nightly once enforcement was enabled.
  - **Skips must cite a bug** — of 49 unconditional skips, 26 already did; the other 23 are on a closed, dated allowlist that new skips can't join and that fails when an entry goes stale.

  ## Evidence

  | Config | Environment | Wall-clock | Failures | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Baseline (CI, W=1) | test-alkem.io | 79.2 min | 2 | — |
  | 69/39, W=5 | test-alkem.io | 56.1 min | 0 | PASS |
  | **94/14, W=5** | **test-alkem.io** | **44.5 min** | 4, all interference | **PASS** |

  `W=10` was tried and failed — setup timeouts and mass-skipped files, one taking 602 s. Resource exhaustion, not interference. **W=5 is the operating point.**

  **client-web verified**: run from this branch against the same environment, it matched the `develop` baseline exactly — 279 tests, 270 passed, 0 failed, the same 2 flaky files, 7 skipped, `exit=0`. That
  exercises the teardown rewrite across its 68 scenario-using files. Its identity path is provably unchanged (`workerCount` defaults to 1; `VITEST_POOL_ID` is never set under Playwright, so slot 0 and
  bare addresses).

  ## Known limits

  - **Notification throughput is a real ceiling.** Parallelism multiplies it roughly linearly with workers; four suites in one day backed up RabbitMQ enough to take the notifications service down.
  - **More server pods will not help** — latency measured identical at rest and under full load; the server idles while the suite runs. The remaining lever is proximity (~43–50 ms RTT from a laptop vs
  ~0.1 ms local). Traefik overhead measured ~0.1 ms.
  - Hazard rules are name/shape blocklists, not structural proofs.
  - The teardown leak summary is **per-worker**, not whole-run — a `worker_threads` consequence; CI greps the whole log.
  - The auto-invite trio's `delay(5000)`-gated assertion is a load-timing hazard: diagnosed, kept serial, not fixed.
  - Mailbox scoping is blocked — MailSlurper has no per-recipient delete, so wipe-all teardown would still race.
  - `callout-reactions.it-spec.ts` interfered once; one entry is below the demotion bar and the ledger surfaces it if it recurs.
  - The ~24 per-area developer scripts consume the changed `lib/` and are **not** covered by this feature's verification.
  - The 23 grandfathered skips are made visible, not fixed — someone still has to do that archaeology.

  ## Raised separately

  - alkem-io/server#6377 — `lookup.*` fields declare `nullable` but throw `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` (37 of 38).
  - #608 — test data not reliably cleaned up.
  - Two diagnosed, unfixed server races: the `ActorContext` cache keying, and the conversion service's empty-roleSet window. Both recorded in the spec.

> - **Fixtures:** `TestScenarioFactory` private Space (self-cleaning) + one MEMO / WHITEBOARD framing callout; the framing document id is the room id.

## Where these tests belong — and why

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `client-web` Playwright nightly | ✗ Dispatch-only (not scheduled); a browser would exist only to mint a cookie; the password would pass through the published report. |
| **`server-api` nightly** | ✓ API-level tests of a backend service, scheduled daily right after `deploy-all-services` (which deploys `collaboration-service`) and the DB reset; same bearer auth as every other call; report published with the rest. |
| New dedicated workflow | ✗ Would duplicate the deploy / cluster-lock / report plumbing for two files. Not needed unless the service gets its own deploy cadence. |

## Cases (each names the regression it catches — see the suite README)

**Both rooms** — admission is the first frame and a Space admin gets `write`; a Space member is admitted and synced; a user outside the private Space is **not** admitted; A's edit converges into B; A's presence is visible to B; a durability request is answered `persisted`; a cold client rehydrates the content **after the room's idle release**.
**Memo** — anonymous handshake refused.
**Whiteboard** — concurrent edits to *different* properties of one element both survive on both sides (per-property `Y.Map`, as `@excalidraw-yjs/element` stores elements); concurrent edits to the *same* property converge to one value.

The two cold-rehydrate cases wait out the service's room idle timeout (30 s default, not overridden on the test cluster; `COLLAB_ROOM_IDLE_RELEASE_MS`). A new client before that is served from memory and proves nothing.
